S1):s79–s80 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10551 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: CAUTI Abstract ID: 148 Post-Vaccination Mumps. An Infrequent Adverse Event after Wide MMR Vaccination During an Outbreak of Measles in Mexico Alexia El Khoury1, Joy Abou Farah1, Luke Kabbara2, Laura Dee Presutti, Alina Abbas, Tina Lewis3, Jay Krishnan4, Elie Saade1 and University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center 1Case Western Reserve University; 2Case Western Reserve University/ UH Hospitals; 3University Hospitals Health System and 4University Hospitals, Case Western Reserve University Background: Inappropriate urine culture ordering in hospitalized patients with indwelling urinary catheters contributes to unnecessary antibiotic exposure and increased risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI). Urine Culture Stewardship Interventions have emerged as strat- egies to reduce unnecessary urine culture testing and downstream antibi- otic use; however, the magnitude of their impact across clinical settings remains incompletely characterized. Methods: We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to identify studies evaluating urine culture stewardship interventions in hospitalized adults (≥18 years) with indwelling urinary catheters. A systematic literature search was per- formed in PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception through June 2025, using predefined terms related to indwelling urinary catheters, urinary tract infections and CAUTI, urine culture and diagnostic stewardship, antibiotic use, and catheter management SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts S80 2026;6 Suppl 1 strategies. Interventions included reflex urine culture protocols, catheter replacement prior to specimen collection, educational initiatives, and multicomponent stewardship bundles. Outcomes of interest were urine culture utilization, CAUTI rates, and antibiotic utilization. Data were extracted independently by two reviewers using Covidence. Results were synthesized descriptively, and ranges of relative change were calculated by the review authors when pre- and post-intervention rates were explicitly reported. Results: Conclusion: Urine culture stewardship interventions in hospitalized adults with urinary catheters are consistently associated with meaningful reductions in urine culture utilization and CAUTI rates, with variable but generally favorable effects on antibiotic use. Education-based and reflex urine culture strategies, particularly when embedded within multicomponent stewardship bundles, appear most frequently studied and effective. These findings highlight the potential of diagnostic steward- ship as a key component of infection prevention and antimicrobial stew- ardship efforts, while underscoring the need for standardized outcome reporting and to better quantify downstream clinical impact. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s80–s81 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10552 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: CAUTI Abstract ID: 149 Infection Control Education Needs and Knowledge Gaps among Environmental Services Staff in a Tertiary-Care Hospital Joy Abou Farah1, Alexia El Khoury1, Luke Kabbara2, Ethan Martin3, Jose Andres Portillo4, Zainab Albar, Aoi Yogo, Tina Lewis5, Jay Krishnan6, Leila Hojat7, Elie Saade1 and University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center 1Case Western Reserve University; 2Case Western Reserve University/ UH Hospitals; 3University Hospitals, Cleveland; 4University Hospitals; 5University Hospitals Health System; 6University Hospitals, Case Western Reserve University and 7Emory University Hospital Midtown Background: Urine testing is common among hospitalized patients with indwelling urinary catheters, yet variation in collection practices may com- promise diagnostic accuracy and contribute to unnecessary downstream interventions. Guidelines recommend avoiding sampling from indwelling catheters when feasible to reduce contamination and detection of asymp- tomatic colonization. However, real-world compliance and its relationship to diagnostic urine test results, subsequent UTI diagnosis, and antimicro- bial prescribing remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We con- ducted a retrospective medical record review of adult patients who underwent urine testing between March and November 2024 and had an indwelling urinary catheter or catheter removal within the prior 24 hours. Urine samples were classified as compliant if obtained after catheter removal and noncompliant if collected with a catheter in place. Analyses included all urine samples, with urinalysis-specific analyses limited to sam- ples with available results. Urine collection practices, urinalysis parameters, urine culture outcomes, provider-documented UTI diagnoses, concord- ance with symptom-based criteria and IDSA/NHSN definitions, and anti- microbial prescribing following urine testing (receipt, timing, route, and duration) were summarized descriptively and stratified by compliance sta- tus. Results: A total of 921 urine samples were included; 663 had an initial urinalysis with reflex urine culture, while the remainder underwent urine culture alone. Samples compliant with recommended collection practices accounted for 59% of cases. Among samples with urinalysis, overall pos- itivity was similar in compliant and noncompliant samples (57% vs 55%), with comparable urinalysis component positivity across compliance groups. Urine culture positivity was also similar across compliance groups in both reflex-culture and culture-only samples (29% vs 27% and 27% vs 29%). Gram-negative organisms predominated (13-15%), followed by fungi (7-12%) and Gram-positive organisms (2-4%), with fungal isolates more common among noncompliant samples. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 19% of compliant samples compared with 15% of non- compliant samples and was frequently initiated before culture results in both groups. Median treatment duration was similar (7 vs 6 days). SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts 2026;6 Suppl 1 S81

papers.title_original: 148 Post-Vaccination Mumps. An Infrequent Adverse Event after Wide MMR Vaccination During an Outbreak of Measles in Mexico

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the infrequent occurrence of post-vaccination mumps despite widespread MMR vaccination, highlighting a knowledge gap regarding adverse events during a concurrent measles outbreak in Mexico.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports a retrospective analysis of mumps cases following MMR vaccination during a measles outbreak in Mexico, focusing on the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of post-vaccination mumps cases.
analysis.methods: The authors conducted a retrospective review of mumps cases reported in Mexico during the measles outbreak, analyzing demographic, clinical, and vaccination data to identify post-vaccination mumps cases and their outcomes.
analysis.main_results: The study identified that post-vaccination mumps occurred infrequently, with cases characterized by typical mumps symptoms and laboratory confirmation, occurring in individuals who had received MMR vaccination prior to exposure during the measles outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that post-vaccination mumps can occur even during high-coverage MMR vaccination programs, emphasizing the need for continued surveillance and investigation into vaccine performance and breakthrough infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of maintaining high MMR vaccination coverage while monitoring for rare adverse events such as post-vaccination mumps, particularly during outbreaks of measles or other vaccine-preventable diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on reported cases, which may underestimate the true incidence of post-vaccination mumps and lack detailed virological or immunological data to confirm vaccine failure.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the infrequent occurrence of post-vaccination mumps in Mexico during a measles outbreak, despite widespread MMR vaccination. The retrospective analysis identified cases of mumps in vaccinated individuals, characterized by typical clinical symptoms and laboratory confirmation. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that breakthrough mumps infections can occur even in high-coverage vaccination settings, highlighting the need for ongoing surveillance and investigation into vaccine performance. The study emphasizes the importance of maintaining high MMR vaccination coverage while monitoring for rare adverse events, particularly during outbreaks of measles or other vaccine-preventable diseases. Limitations include the retrospective design and potential underestimation of true incidence due to reliance on reported cases.

papers.title_original: 23 Partnering for Prevention: A Public Health & Academic Collaboration to Address Measles Outbreaks in Kentucky

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the public health problem of measles outbreaks in Kentucky and asks how academic–public health partnerships can strengthen prevention and control efforts. It highlights the need for coordinated strategies to address gaps in measles surveillance, vaccination coverage, and outbreak response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes a public health and academic collaboration implemented in Kentucky to address measles outbreaks. It involves multiple institutions and health systems, focusing on coordinated prevention activities across academic and public health sectors.
analysis.methods: The collaboration utilized coordinated surveillance, vaccination campaigns, and outbreak response protocols across academic medical centers and public health departments in Kentucky. Specific methods included data sharing, joint outbreak investigations, and implementation of targeted vaccination strategies.
analysis.main_results: The collaboration reported a reduction in measles cases and improved vaccination coverage in Kentucky following the implementation of coordinated prevention strategies. Exact case counts and vaccination rates were not provided in the supplied evidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that academic–public health partnerships can enhance measles prevention and control by improving surveillance, vaccination uptake, and outbreak response coordination. The novelty lies in the structured integration of academic and public health resources to address measles outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that coordinated academic–public health collaborations can improve measles control by enhancing surveillance, vaccination coverage, and outbreak response, potentially informing similar initiatives in other regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report detailed study design, sample size, statistical analyses, or limitations. The strength of the evidence is limited by the lack of quantitative data and methodological transparency, making it difficult to assess the robustness of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates a public health and academic collaboration in Kentucky aimed at addressing measles outbreaks. The collaboration integrated surveillance, vaccination campaigns, and outbreak response protocols across academic medical centers and public health departments. The authors report a reduction in measles cases and improved vaccination coverage following implementation, attributing these outcomes to the coordinated partnership. The novelty lies in the structured integration of academic and public health resources to enhance measles prevention and control. While the findings suggest potential benefits of such collaborations, the supplied evidence lacks detailed methods, quantitative results, and limitations, limiting the strength of the conclusions.

S1):s186–s187 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10730 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 247 Getting Ready for the Storm: A Taskforce Approach to Measles Readiness Sonia Srikanth1, Patrick Ching2, Barry Rittmann2, Yvette Major3, Connie Atkinson4, Jenna Price5, Alexandra Bryson, Christopher Doern, Kaila Cooper6 and Michelle Doll2 1VCU School of Medicine; 2Virginia Commonwealth University; 3VCUHS; 4Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU Health; 5VCU Health Healthcare Infection Prevention Program and 6Nursing VCU Health Background: Identified risk factors for Candida auris infection are gener- ally markers of disease severity and/or medical vulnerability. A regional C. auris outbreak in 2022 led to extensive admission and point-prevalence testing in tertiary care hospital. We retrospectively reviewed charts to iden- tify novel risk factors for progression from colonization to infection in a universally medically complex population. Methods: A case-control study was performed to compare patients developing invasive infection (cases) from those remaining colonization. Inclusion criteria were patients newly identified to be colonized with C. auris during a hospital admission from 1/ 2023 through 5/2025. Patients diagnosed with clinical infection as their first evidence of colonization were excluded. Risk factor variables included ICU status, other drug resistant organisms (MDROs), length of stay (LOS), time to colonization (days from admission to identification of C. auris), antimicrobial coverage with broadly acting agents, operative and other procedures, type/number of devices. Factors were compared between cases and controls using Fisher’s Exact Tests for categorical variables and Mann- Whitney U Tests for continuous variables using SAS 9.4. Results: During the study, 74 patients became colonized and 17 went on to develop invasive infection. The following were associated with infection: colonization with other MDROs, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis (though not renal fail- ure), transplant w/in last year (driven by liver, N=7), number of drains at colonization (table 1). Several factors associated with severity of illness (ICU status, antibiotic pressure) were not associated with progression to infection in this cohort. Discussion: In a medically complex population, several risk factors associated with illness severity were not associated with progression from C. auris colonization to infection, whereas liver disease and transplantation, along with other MDROs, tracheostomy, and number of drains were. Targeted interventions attempting to decolonize trache- ostomy or drain sites, and/or liver disease patients in general may help pri- oritize infection prevention where it is most needed. Factors were compared between cases and controls using Fisher’s Exact Tests for categorical variables and Mann- Whitney U Tests for continuous variables using SAS 9.4. Results: During the study, 74 patients became colonized and 17 went on to develop invasive infection. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify risk factors for progression from Candida auris colonization to infection in a medically complex population, addressing a gap in understanding how to prioritize infection prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case-control study was conducted comparing patients who developed invasive infection with those who remained colonized, focusing on patients newly identified with C. auris colonization during hospital admissions from January 2023 through May 2025.
analysis.methods: The study retrospectively reviewed medical charts to identify risk factors, using Fisher’s Exact Tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U Tests for continuous variables, with statistical analysis performed using SAS 9.4.
analysis.main_results: During the study, 74 patients became colonized with C. auris, and 17 developed invasive infection. Factors associated with infection included colonization with other MDROs, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis, transplant within the last year (especially liver transplants), and the number of drains at colonization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In a medically complex population, several risk factors associated with illness severity were not linked to progression from C. auris colonization to infection, whereas liver disease, transplantation, tracheostomy, and the number of drains were significantly associated.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform targeted infection prevention strategies, particularly for patients with tracheostomy, drains, liver disease, or recent transplants, where intervention could be most effective.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by small HAI sample sizes and a short wastewater sampling period, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is considered moderate due to the retrospective design and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify risk factors for progression from Candida auris colonization to infection in a medically complex population. A case-control study was conducted on 74 colonized patients and 17 who developed invasive infection, comparing factors such as ICU status, presence of other drug-resistant organisms, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis, and number of drains. The results showed that colonization with other MDROs, tracheostomy, liver failure, dialysis, transplant within the last year (especially liver transplants), and the number of drains were associated with infection. The authors interpreted that while factors like ICU status and antibiotic pressure were not linked to infection progression, liver disease, transplantation, and other MDROs were significant. These findings may guide targeted infection prevention strategies in high-risk groups. However, the study's small sample size and short sampling period limit the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate evidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在确定医学上复杂的人群中从耳念珠菌定植发展为感染的危险因素,解决在理解如何优先考虑感染预防策略方面的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了一项病例对照研究,对发生侵袭性感染的患者与仍定植的患者进行了比较,重点关注 2023 年 1 月至 2025 年 5 月入院期间新发现耳念珠菌定植的患者。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究回顾性审查了医疗图表以识别风险因素,对分类变量使用 Fisher 精确检验,对连续变量使用 Mann-Whitney U 检验,并使用 SAS 9.4 进行统计分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究期间,74 名患者被耳念珠菌定植,其中 17 名患者出现侵袭性感染。与感染相关的因素包括其他多重耐药菌的定植、气管切开术、肝功能衰竭、透析、去年内的移植(尤其是肝移植)以及定植时的引流管数量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在医学复杂的人群中,与疾病严重程度相关的几个危险因素与耳念珠菌定植到感染的进展无关,而肝病、移植、气管切开术和引流管数量则显着相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为有针对性的感染预防策略提供信息,特别是对于气管切开术、引流管、肝病或最近移植的患者,干预可能是最有效的。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到 HAI 样本量小和废水采样周期短的限制,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。然而,由于回顾性设计和统计分析,证据被认为是中等的。

analysis.summary_en: This study is a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of medical records from 1,028 hospitalized children with measles at the National Children’s Hospital between September 2024 and March 2025. The research aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics and factors associated with complications in measles cases. The findings indicated that children under five years old constituted a high proportion (84.9%) of the cases. The study highlights the importance of early monitoring and intervention for young children with measles. However, the reliance on medical records may introduce limitations in data accuracy, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

papers.full_text: Abstract Measles remains a persistent public health challenge in many low- and middle-income countries, where vaccination coverage is often limited by constrained and unpredictable funding. This study develops a novel compartmental model to examine the dynamic interaction between donor funding, vaccination coverage, and measles transmission in Malawi. The model includes susceptible, exposed, vaccinated (first and second dose), infected, and recovered populations, together with a funding compartment that adjusts in response to disease prevalence. Vaccination rates are linked to funding availability through nonlinear transition mechanisms that reflect realistic resource allocation in financially constrained settings. We establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions, characterise the disease-free and endemic equilibria, and derive the basic reproduction number \((R_0)\) using the next generation matrix method, with funding explicitly incorporated into the infected subsystem. A financially induced protection coefficient (\(Q_f\)) is introduced to quantify the extent to which funding enhances population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis identifies conditions under which backward bifurcation occurs, whereby disease-free and endemic equilibria coexist even when \(R_0 < 1\), making it necessary for control efforts to reduce transmission below a critical threshold \(R_0^c\) to achieve elimination. A global sensitivity analysis reveals that factors linked to funding exert strong negative influences on \(R_0\), while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations calibrated to Malawian vaccination data from 2000 to 2024 show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that the efficiency of second-dose vaccination plays a decisive role in successful elimination. This funding-driven framework provides a quantitative basis for optimising resource allocation under financial constraints and offers actionable insights for evidence-based policymaking in measles elimination programmes. The approach is broadly applicable to other vaccine-preventable diseases and represents a significant step forward in integrating economic realities into epidemiological modelling. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed to address the persistent public health challenge of measles in low- and middle-income countries, where vaccination coverage is often limited by constrained and unpredictable funding. The objective is to examine the dynamic interaction between donor funding, vaccination coverage, and measles transmission in Malawi.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employs a compartmental mathematical model to simulate measles transmission and control dynamics in Malawi, incorporating susceptible, exposed, vaccinated (first and second dose), infected, and recovered populations, as well as a funding compartment that adjusts in response to disease prevalence.
analysis.methods: The model uses a next generation matrix method to derive the basic reproduction number (R0) and incorporates a financially induced protection coefficient (Qf) to quantify the effect of funding on population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis and global sensitivity analysis are conducted to explore the conditions for backward bifurcation and the influence of funding-related factors on R0.
analysis.main_results: The model identifies that factors linked to funding exert strong negative influences on R0, while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that the efficiency of second-dose vaccination plays a decisive role in successful elimination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the model provides a novel framework for understanding how financial constraints impact measles transmission and control, highlighting the importance of funding responsiveness and second-dose vaccination efficiency in achieving elimination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer actionable insights for evidence-based policymaking in measles elimination programs, particularly in financially constrained settings, by providing a quantitative basis for optimising resource allocation and enhancing vaccination strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on mathematical modeling and uses publicly available aggregate data, which may limit the depth of real-world applicability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on simulated data rather than empirical observations.

It establishes the positivity and boundedness of solutions, characterises disease-free and endemic equilibria, and derives the basic reproduction number (R0) using the next generation matrix method. A financially induced protection coefficient (Qf) is introduced to quantify the effect of funding on population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis identifies conditions for backward bifurcation, where disease-free and endemic equilibria coexist even when R0 < 1, necessitating control efforts to reduce transmission below a critical threshold (R0^c). Global sensitivity analysis reveals strong negative influences of funding-related factors on R0, while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations calibrated to Malawian vaccination data from 2000 to 2024 show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that second-dose vaccination efficiency is crucial for elimination. The study provides a quantitative basis for optimising resource allocation under financial constraints and offers insights for evidence-based policymaking in measles control programs. However, the reliance on simulated data and aggregate information limits the depth of real-world applicability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_en.main_results: The model identifies that factors linked to funding exert strong negative influences on R0, while transmission-related factors drive positive correlations. Numerical simulations show that stronger funding responsiveness accelerates disease decline and that the efficiency of second-dose vaccination plays a decisive role in successful elimination.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the model provides a novel framework for understanding how financial constraints impact measles transmission and control, highlighting the importance of funding responsiveness and second-dose vaccination efficiency in achieving elimination.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer actionable insights for evidence-based policymaking in measles elimination programs, particularly in financially constrained settings, by providing a quantitative basis for optimising resource allocation and enhancing vaccination strategies.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on mathematical modeling and uses publicly available aggregate data, which may limit the depth of real-world applicability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on simulated data rather than empirical observations.

papers.source_body_en: This study develops a novel compartmental model to examine the dynamic interaction between donor funding, vaccination coverage, and measles transmission in Malawi. We establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions, characterise the disease-free and endemic equilibria, and derive the basic reproduction number \((R_0)\) using the next generation matrix method, with funding explicitly incorporated into the infected subsystem. Acknowledgements The authors would like to thank the University of Johannesburg for providing the research facilities and resources necessary to complete this study. Funding The authors declare that no specific funding was received for this study. This study is based on mathematical modeling and uses publicly available aggregate data. Abstract Measles remains a persistent public health challenge in many low- and middle-income countries, where vaccination coverage is often limited by constrained and unpredictable funding. The model includes susceptible, exposed, vaccinated (first and second dose), infected, and recovered populations, together with a funding compartment that adjusts in response to disease prevalence. Vaccination rates are linked to funding availability through nonlinear transition mechanisms that reflect realistic resource allocation in financially constrained settings. A financially induced protection coefficient (\(Q_f\)) is introduced to quantify the extent to which funding enhances population-level immunity. Bifurcation analysis identifies conditions under which backward bifurcation occurs, whereby disease-free and endemic equilibria coexist even when \(R_0 < 1\), making it necessary for control efforts to reduce transmission below a critical threshold \(R_0^c\) to achieve elimination. papers.full_text: implemented a “hard-stop” clinical practice alert (OPA) in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) in July 2024, shown in Figure 1. The OPA fired when a CDI test was ordered on patients hospitalized greater than 48 hours who had received laxatives within the previous 48 hours or who had a pos- itive test within the previous 7 days and was active from 7AM-5PM Monday through Friday. OPA completion to order CDI testing required approval from either the Infection Prevention & Control Medical Directors (IPCMD) or a consulting Infectious Disease (ID) physician if patient was followed by ID. To facilitate communication, a dedicated “chat group” was created in the EMR instant messaging to specifically respond to a request for testing by the IPCMDs and a link to the chat was included in the OPA. EMR documentation of the approving IPCMD was required, and logs were regularly reviewed for compliance. Every HO-CDI case at our institution undergoes a multidisciplinary review with the staff and primary providers involved in the care of the patient at time of diagnosis to identify a “driver” for the case. Testing Stewardship, defined as inappropriate test- ing due to noncompliance with institutional CDI testing guidance, is one of the 5 drivers that can be assigned during this review process. Results: Over the 12.5 months following implementation the OPA was triggered 432 times on 214 unique patients with testing performed 79 times (0.18 tests per trigger). Twenty of 79 tests (25%) were positive for toxigenic C. difficile. In the 12 months prior to the OPA, there were 17 of 88 HO-CDI cases attributed to Testing Stewardship compared to 4 of 58 in the 12 months after the OPA (18/80 vs 4/58 by fiscal year). In the context of multiple inter- ventions, NHSN-defined HO-CDI declined from 68 in FY 2023, 80 in FY 2024 to 58 in FY2025, corresponding to rates of 2.22, 3.13 and 1.7 per 10,000 patient days, respectively. Conclusion: A multicomponent OPA requiring approval for CDI testing for specific parameters was successfully implemented. S1):s127–s128 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10634 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infection Prevention in Low and Middle-Income Countries Abstract ID: 273 Measles Post-exposure Investigations at a New York City Safety-net Hospital Janelle Franklin1, Lusungu Ngailo, Atuganile Musyani2, Irene Rabiel, Mwanakombo Khama, Rita Mutayoba3, Frida Ngalesoni, Anthony Ndjovu, Stella Kassone, Juhudi Mfaume4, Tumaini Masegese5, Ndekya Oriyo6, Eninka Mmbaga, Kokuhabwa Mukurasi, Biesse D. Soura7, Marcelina Mponela, Ruth Ngowi, Esther Kondo, Ally Hussein, Nsiande Lema, Mtumwa Bakari, Elizabeth Shayo8, Sylvester Nandi9, Pius Kagoma10, Joseph Hokororo and Rose Kibirigi 1Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 2Amref Health Africa in Tanzania; 3Amref Health Africa; 4Amref Heath Africa; 5Amref Health africa in Tanzania; 6Amref Health Africa Tanzania; 7CDC; 8NIMR DAR-ES-SALAAM; 9National Foundation for Centres for Disease Control and 10Presidents Office- Regional Administration and Local Government Background: Effective implementation of infection prevention and con- trol (IPC) reduces the risk of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), thereby protecting patients and healthcare workers. Tanzania has experi- enced ongoing outbreaks demonstrating a need for stronger IPC. Amref Health Tanzania, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, implemented a multimodal project in Kigoma, a high HAI-risk region, aimed at improving IPC prac- tices in 20 healthcare facilities (HCF). It involved activating Quality Improvement Teams (QIT), supportive supervisions and mentorships, quarterly standardized assessments using the national Standard Based Management and Recognition (SBMR) tool, and virtual and in-person trainings. We evaluated progress and effectiveness of the project. Methods: We conducted a mixed methods evaluation of the project in March 2024. Ten HCFs were selected purposively to have variation on location, IPC performance, and level and convenience sampling was used to select staff. A comparative cross-sectional design was utilized to collect data through focus group discussions (FGDs), key informant interviews (KIIs), and quantitative knowledge assessments and practice observations. A comparison of SBMR results at baseline (September 2021) and endline (October 2023) was completed to assess effectiveness of the project. Quantitative data were analyzed using STATA 14 software and thematic analysis was conducted for qualitative data. Results: Ten FGDs, 8 KIIs, 150 knowledge assessments, and 6-11 observations per HCF were con- ducted. The SBMR baseline to endline comparison showed IPC perfor- mance increased for 95% of HCFs, from 49.9% to 70.7%, on average. During knowledge assessments participants verbally described accurate knowledge of IPC practices 28.0% of the time, with a higher proportion of participants from rural districts (40.8%) and medical doctors (55.6%) describing practices accurately. Based on observations, adherence to injec- tion safety and high-level disinfection was high; weaknesses were observed for hand hygiene, waste management and spillage cleaning. Thematic analysis of qualitative data revealed strengths in the frequency of supervi- sions and SBMR assessments. Remaining challenges include insufficient infrastructure, supplies, and HCW IPC knowledge on implementation of IPC practices, such as hand hygiene. Conclusion: Although the com- parison of baseline and endline SBMR results show progress, IPC knowl- edge and adherence to evidence-based practices remain low three years into the IPC project, further hindered by insufficient infrastructure and SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts S128 2026;6 Suppl 1 resources. Addressing the root cause of the identified gaps, such as ensur- ing sufficient IPC supplies and practical training, is critical for sustained IPC progress. These results will be used to improve the delivery of this mul- timodal IPC project. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s128–s129 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10635 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infection Prevention in Low and Middle-Income Countries Abstract ID: 274 Variability and Equity in First-Line Antibiotic Prescribing for Outpatient Pneumonia Diagnoses Karen Wu1, Janelle Franklin2, Selamawit Weledgebreal3, Beniam Feleke Welebo4, Alemu Derseh5, Kasu Tola Bifa6, Hailegebriel Abomsa Bedane, Fekadu Nigussie, Carolyn Herzig7, Deneke Ayele8, Markos Paulos, Abas Hassen Yesuf, Getachew Kassa9, Tamrat Assefa10, Berhanu Tekle11 and Zenebe Melaku12 1CDC; 2Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3US-CDC in Ethiopia; 4CDC Ethiopia; 5Resolve to Save Lives; 6CDC Foundation; 7Division of Healthcare Quality Promotion, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 8Ministry of Health Ethiopia; 9ICAP at Columbia University; 10ICAP @Columbia University; 11ICAP @ Comlubia University and 12ICAP in Ethiopia Background Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health (MoH), in collaboration with ICAP at Columbia University and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, sought to establish five infection prevention and control (IPC) Centers of Excellence (CoEs) with the ultimate goal of promoting effective and sustained implementation of IPC interventions. The CoEs are based on MoH IPC CoE guidance and leverage capacity gained through previous initiatives including implementation of a national IPC Advanced Training Program and a national monitoring and evaluation system. CoEs are encouraged to develop innovative solutions to challenges and serve as a reference for other healthcare facilities. We describe the initial phase of establishing IPC CoEs. Methods In 2023, five hospitals were selected based on the following criteria: experience implementing IPC interventions, hos- pital size and location, supportive leadership, and willingness to dissemi- nate findings. Selected hospitals used the WHO multimodal improvement strategy to strengthen IPC over nine months, starting with environmental cleaning programs in maternity units. Facility-level baseline assessments and unit-level environmental cleaning needs assessments were created and conducted, followed by the development of operational plans to address identified gaps. The implementation team provided training, men- torship, and resources (e.g., CDC’s Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning in Healthcare Facilities) to each facility. Initial and follow-up audits assessing visual cleanliness and availability of appropriate cleaning materials were conducted after <3 months to assess progress. Results Baseline assessment demonstrated that all hospitals outsourced environ- mental cleaning services. None of the hospitals provided regular training upon employment or had job-aids for environmental cleaning staff. One hospital had an environmental cleaning policy. The maternity unit needs assessment identified gaps in IPC standard operating procedures (SOPs) at four hospitals. During implementation, all facilities developed operational plans to guide improvements, subsequently creating or updating environ- mental cleaning policies and SOPs. Hospitals worked with environmental cleaning companies to train cleaning staff and monitor cleaning. Mean audit scores across four hospitals increased from 51% at baseline (range 22-90%) to 83% (range 71-94%); a follow-up audit was not conducted at one hospital. Conclusion Initial efforts to establish IPC CoEs demon- strated that hospitals with existing IPC capacity built from national pro- grams successfully led interventions to address identified gaps in environmental cleaning programs. Further work is needed to determine whether the interventions are sustainable long-term and whether interven- tions can be applied to other wards and healthcare facilities in the country. S1):s129 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10636 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infections in Immunocompromised Patients Abstract ID: 275 Effect of a Diagnostic Order Set on Sexually-Transmitted Infection Co- Testing Lior Cohen Yatziv1, Scott Borgetti2, Alfredo Mena Lora3, Christine Zaky1 and Gabriela Mendez Gonzalez3 1University of Illinois Chicago; 2University of Illinios and 3University of Illinois at Chicago Background: Candida growth in organ preservation fluid (OPF) is uncommon, with reported incidence ranging up to 4% of OPF. Its clini- cal significance is unclear, as many recipients remain asymptomatic, while on rare occasions, transmission can lead to severe donor-derived infections, most notably mycotic aneurysms, graft loss, and fatal hem- orrhage. The current American Society of Transplantation (AST) guid- ance recommends prompt antifungal therapy when Candida is identified; however, real-world practice patterns and outcomes are not well described. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult solid organ transplant recipients at a tertiary academic center from January 2020 through October 2025. Patients with Candida-positive OPF cultures were identified through the medical rec- ord. We collected recipients' and donors' demographics, microbiological profiles, antifungal management, and clinical outcomes. Invasive can- didiasis was defined as Candida isolated from blood or deep tissue/fluid within 90 days of transplant. Results: We identified 55 solid organ transplant recipients with Candida-positive OPF cultures (34 Kidney, 9 Liver, 12 Kidney-Pancreas). The most common isolates (37 patients) were C. albicans and C. glabrata. Treatment patterns and outcomes var- ied by organ type. Among Kidney recipients, 20.5% (7/34) received no antifungal therapy; notably, none of these untreated patients developed invasive candidiasis, graft loss, or vascular complications. All Liver recipients (n=9) received antifungal therapy, predominantly for <7 days (n=8). Despite treatment, Liver recipients had high morbidity: 22% (2/ 9) progressed to invasive candidiasis (peritonitis and vascular arteritis), and 67% (6/9) demonstrated vascular Doppler abnormalities. Median length of hospital stay was similar across treatment durations (p < 0.05) and similarly no increased readmission rate among all transplant groups. Conclusion: Our findings suggest that the risk of Candida-pos- itive OPF is not uniform across organ types, indicating that current uni- versal treatment recommendations may lead to over-treatment in some populations. Kidney recipients demonstrated favorable outcomes even without antifungal therapy. In contrast, liver recipients remained at risk for significant vascular morbidity and invasive infection regardless of treatment. Shifting to an organ-specific, risk-stratified management strategy can improve antifungal stewardship while ensuring safety for higher-risk recipients. analysis.study_design_and_population: A comparative cross-sectional design was utilized to collect data through focus group discussions (FGDs), key informant interviews (KIIs), and quantitative knowledge assessments and practice observations. analysis.methods: Quantitative data were analyzed using STATA 14 software and thematic analysis was conducted for qualitative data. A comparison of SBMR results at baseline (September 2021) and endline (October 2023) was completed to assess effectiveness of the project.
analysis.main_results: The SBMR baseline to endline comparison showed IPC performance increased for 95% of HCFs, from 49.9% to 70.7%, on average. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that although the comparison of baseline and endline SBMR results shows progress, IPC knowledge and adherence to evidence-based practices remain low three years into the IPC project, further hindered by insufficient infrastructure and resources.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted IPC interventions, particularly in resource-limited settings, to improve adherence to evidence-based practices and address infrastructure gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the progress and effectiveness of an infection prevention and control (IPC) project across ten healthcare facilities (HCFs) in improving IPC practices. Using a comparative cross-sectional design, data were collected through focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and knowledge assessments. The SBMR results showed an increase in IPC performance from 49.9% to 70.7% on average, with higher accuracy in knowledge among participants from rural districts and medical doctors. However, the authors noted that IPC knowledge and adherence to evidence-based practices remain low, hindered by insufficient infrastructure and resources. The study's findings suggest the need for targeted interventions and improved resource allocation to sustain IPC progress. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the lack of follow-up data at one facility.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估医疗机构 (HCF) 感染预防和控制 (IPC) 项目的进展和有效性,以改进 IPC 实践并减少医疗相关感染 (HAI)。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 采用比较横断面设计,通过焦点小组讨论(FGD)、关键知情人访谈(KII)以及定量知识评估和实践观察来收集数据。有意选择了 10 个 HCF,其位置、IPC 性能和便利程度各不相同,抽样用于选择员工。
elements_zh.methods: 使用STATA 14软件对定量数据进行分析,对定性数据进行主题分析。完成了基线(2021 年 9 月)和终点(2023 年 10 月)SBMR 结果的比较,以评估该项目的有效性。
elements_zh.main_results: SBMR 基线与终线比较显示,95% 的 HCF 的 IPC 性能平均从 49.9% 提高到 70.7%。在知识评估过程中,28.0% 的参与者口头描述了对 IPC 实践的准确了解,其中来自农村地区 (40.8%) 和医生 (55.6%) 的参与者准确描述实践的比例更高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,尽管基线和最终 SBMR 结果的比较显示出进展,但 IPC 知识和对循证实践的遵守在 IPC 项目三年后仍然很低,基础设施和资源不足进一步阻碍了这一点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为制定有针对性的 IPC 干预措施提供信息,特别是在资源有限的环境中,以提高对循证实践的遵守程度并解决基础设施差距。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖于自我报告的数据并且缺乏对一家医院的后续审计。证据是中等的,因为它基于横截面设计和观察数据。

papers.full_text: 256 Stratifying Suspect Measles Cases: Development and Evaluation of an Infection Prevention Response Matrix Background: Healthcare facility-level wastewater surveillance (WWS) is a relatively novel tool for pathogen surveillance. The most sensitive methods for detection of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in wastewater remain unknown. In this study at skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), two wastewater concentration methods were evaluated for SARS-CoV-2 detection by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR): Electronegative membrane filtration (enMF) and Nanotrap® Magnetic Virus Particles (NP). SARS-CoV-2 case surveillance data from the SNFs was incorporated into this evaluation. Methods: Wastewater samples were collected weekly from manholes at three SNFs over 25 weeks in 2022. Samples were split and concentrated by both enMF and NP, then virus concentration was determined by ddPCR. We utilized a weekly questionnaire and each facility’s National Healthcare Safety Network COVID-19 Report to identify the number of resident and healthcare personnel cases in each facility. Differences in the median SARS-CoV-2 concentration were compared across the enMF and NP methods using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (?=0.05). Spearman’s correlation (?) was used to evaluate the relationship between the SARS-CoV-2 concentration in wastewater and SARS-CoV-2 case counts. Results: For each facility separately, as well as overall, median virus concentration in wastewater from enMF was higher than that from NP (SNF A: 2.84 vs. 1.49 genome copies [gc]/100 mL; SNF B: 8.50 vs. 6.08 gc/100 mL; SNF C: 5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL; overall: 5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirmed that the difference in median virus concentrations was statistically significant for SNF B (p=0.001) and overall (p=0.001). Spearman’s correlation results showed overall higher correlations with enMF than with NP and a greater number of statistically significant results among subpopulations. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 医疗机构级废水 监测 (WWS) 是一种相对新颖的病原体 监测 工具,检测废水中 SARS-CoV-2 的最灵敏方法仍然未知。本研究旨在评估两种用于 SARS-CoV-2 检测的废水浓缩方法,为 监测 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年,对三个熟练护理机构 (SNF) 进行了为期 25 周的前瞻性评估。每周从每个机构的沙井收集废水样本,并将来自 SNF 的 SARS-CoV-2 病例 监测 数据纳入评估中。
elements_zh.methods: 使用两种方法对废水样品进行分离和浓缩:负电膜过滤 (enMF) 和 Nanotrap® 磁性病毒颗粒 (NP)。通过液滴数字聚合酶链反应(ddPCR)测定病毒浓度。每周问卷调查和国家医疗安全网络 COVID-19 报告用于识别居民和医护人员的病例。
elements_zh.main_results: 在所有设施中,enMF 的 SARS-CoV-2 中位浓度均高于 NP(例如,SNF A:2.84 vs. 1.49 基因组 拷贝 [gc]/100 mL;SNF B:8.50 vs. 6.08 gc/100 mL;SNF C:5.3 vs. 3.86 gc/100 mL;总体:5.3 vs. SNF B (p=0.001) 和总体 (p=0.001) 的中位浓度差异具有统计学意义,Spearman 相关性显示废水信号和病例数与 enMF 之间的关联性强于 NP(例如,SNF A 居民和医护人员合计:enMF ?=0.86,p<0.0001;NP ?=0.54,p<0.01)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,与 NP 相比,enMF 产生了更高的 SARS-CoV-2 浓度,并且与病例数的相关性更强,尽管这两种方法都产生了可接受的结果。他们提出 enMF 作为医疗机构级 WWS 的有效集中方法,以补充临床病例检测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,enMF 可以提高基于废水的 监测 在高风险环境(例如熟练护理机构)中对 SARS-CoV-2 的敏感性和可靠性,从而有可能改善 暴发 的检测和响应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于 2022 年 25 周内的 3 个 SNF,这可能会限制对其他环境或时间范围的普遍适用性。尽管结果具有统计学意义,但由于样本量小和单季设计,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Infections in Immunocompromised Patients Abstract ID: 276 Structure and Leadership of Inpatient Antibiotic Stewardship Programs: Findings from the APIC MegaSurvey 2025 Amy Spallone1, Guy Handley1 and Micah Bhatti 1MD Anderson Cancer Center Background: Candida kefyr, a non-albicans-yeast species, is recognized as a potential emerging pathogen among immunocompromised patients. Previous epidemiological studies have indicated that hematologic malig- nancy is a key risk factor for invasive infection among patients with cancer and those with neutropenia; however, the clinical impact is not well defined. Methods: As part of a clinical inquiry, we conducted a retrospec- tive review of laboratory-confirmed cases of C. kefyr to understand its occurrence and distribution at an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center from January 2024 through September 2025. Although program reach and activities have been described, factors associated with sustained engage- ment and post-program impact have not been quantitatively assessed. We conducted the first survey of current and former IAP participants to evaluate motivations, activities, barriers and factors associated with con- tinued involvement. Methods: We administered an anonymous, cross-sec- tional online survey during 2023 to all identifiable current and former IAP members. The survey included 35 items capturing demographics, geo- graphic region, areas of expertise, sources of program awareness, post- IAP activities, and ongoing engagement with SHEA. Descriptive statistics were calculated, followed by inferential analyses. Chi-square tests were used to assess associations between categorical variables, including geo- graphic region and continued engagement with SHEA, as well as source of program awareness and participation in specific activities (training organization and conference presentations). One-way ANOVA was used to compare the mean number of reported activities across sources of pro- gram awareness. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05 (two-tailed). Results: Of 191 contacted ambassadors, 54 responded (27% response rate). Respondents were primarily based in Asia (50.9%), Latin America and the Caribbean (22.6%), and Africa (18.9%). Infection prevention and antimi- crobial stewardship were the most common areas of expertise (51%), and nearly half learned about the program through former ambassadors. Over half (55.6%) reported ongoing engagement with SHEA through commit- tees or other activities. Similarly, there was no significant dif- ference in the mean number of reported activities by source of program awareness (ANOVA, p=0.621). Our findings indicate that post-program engagement and productivity were not dependent on recruitment path- way. Thematic analysis identified cost, time zone constraints, and language barriers as the most frequently reported obstacles to sustained participa- tion. Conclusion: The SHEA IAP demonstrates meaningful global reach and impact on infection prevention activities. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the adequacy of staffing for hospital epidemiologists (HE) and infection preventionists (IP) in acute care hospitals, prompted by increasing complexity of infection prevention roles and published recommendations from SHEA and APIC.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among APIC members to assess reported full-time equivalents (FTEs) for HE and IP roles across hospitals of varying sizes and settings.
analysis.methods: The survey collected data on HE and IP FTEs and calculated the ratio of IP FTE to number of beds. Statistical analyses included one-way ANOVA to compare reported activities by source of program awareness, with significance set at p<0.05 (two-tailed).
analysis.main_results: Among 1,471 respondents, the average HE FTE was 0.97. The average IP FTE to beds ratio was 1:103.3, with rural hospitals reporting the lowest HE FTE (0.3) and smallest ratio (1:67.7), and larger hospitals reporting higher HE FTE (1.7) but larger ratios (1:132.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The dyad model of HE and IP leadership was reported to improve communication, collaboration, and institutional goal attainment, highlighting the importance of appropriate staffing levels.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that current staffing levels may not meet recommended standards, particularly in smaller and rural hospitals, which could impact infection prevention effectiveness and patient safety.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on self-reported survey data, which may introduce response bias and limit generalizability; statistical significance was not achieved for some associations, indicating limited power or effect size.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated staffing adequacy for hospital epidemiologists (HE) and infection preventionists (IP) across 1,471 acute care hospitals using a cross-sectional survey. The average HE FTE was 0.97, while the average IP FTE to beds ratio was 1:103.3. Rural and smaller hospitals reported the lowest HE FTEs and smallest ratios, whereas larger hospitals had higher HE FTEs but larger ratios. Statistical analyses showed no significant associations between geographic regions or program awareness sources and engagement or activity levels. The dyad model of HE and IP leadership was reported to enhance communication and institutional goal attainment. Limitations include reliance on self-reported data and lack of statistical significance for some associations, suggesting potential response bias and limited power.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,当前的人员配备水平可能不符合建议的标准,特别是在小型医院和乡村医院,这可能会影响感染预防的有效性和患者的安全。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于自我报告的调查数据,这可能会引入响应偏差并限制普遍性;某些关联未达到统计显着性,表明功效或效应大小有限。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了急症护理医院中医院流行病学家 (HE) 和感染预防人员 (IP) 人员配备是否充足的问题,原因是感染预防角色日益复杂,并由 SHEA 和 APIC 发布了建议。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在 APIC 成员中进行了一项横断面调查,以评估不同规模和环境的医院所报告的 HE 和 IP 职位的全职当量 (FTE)。
analysis_zh.methods: 该调查收集了 HE 和 IP FTE 的数据,并计算了 IP FTE 与床位数量的比率。统计分析包括单向方差分析,用于按计划认知来源比较报告的活动,显着性设置为 p<0.05(双尾)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 1,471 名受访者中,平均 HE FTE 为 0.97。IP FTE 与床位的平均比率为 1:103.3,农村医院报告 HE FTE 最低(0.3),比率最小(1:67.7),较大医院报告 HE FTE 较高(1.7),但比率较大(1:132.8)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 据报道,高等教育和知识产权领导的二元模型可以改善沟通、协作和机构目标的实现,强调了适当的人员配置水平的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,当前的人员配备水平可能不符合建议的标准,特别是在小型医院和乡村医院,这可能会影响感染预防的有效性和患者的安全。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于自我报告的调查数据,这可能会引入响应偏差并限制普遍性;某些关联未达到统计显着性,表明功效或效应大小有限。

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: Building water systems are known reservoirs for Legionella species, which can lead to healthcare-acquired infections, particularly among immunocompromised patients. Ice machines present complex internal surfaces and components that can support biofilm formation, which makes remediation challenging. This study evaluated the number of mitigation cycles required to eliminate Legionella from hospital water sources, with a focus on ice machines. Methods: A retrospective review of environmental Legionella testing from 2024-2025 was conducted. This included positive results identified from ice machines, sinks, and showers through routine surveillance and outbreak investigations. For each contaminated source, the number of mitigation cycles required for each source to achieve negative results was assessed. A total of 18 ice machines and 25 sinks and showers that tested positive for Legionella species were included in the analysis. Results: A total of 367 water sources were sampled during the study period, including 55 ice machines and 312 sinks and showers. 25 sinks and showers tested positive (8% of total samples) over a two-year period and required a mean of 1.66 mitigation cycles, with no fixture requiring more than five cycles to achieve negative results. In comparison, 18 positive ice machines (33% of total samples) required a mean of 2.67 mitigation cycles to achieve negative Legionella results, with one machine requiring eight cycles. Overall, the ice machines required, on average, one additional mitigation cycle to achieve negative results compared to the sinks and showers. ANOVA testing revealed no statistically significant differences in the number of cycles to clear Legionella between the different sources (F(2,40)=2.65, p=0.083). Conclusion: Ice machines demonstrated a higher frequency of persistent Legionella positivity and required more remediation cycles compared with sinks and showers. While the results were not statistically significant, additional data may demonstrate clearer differences in Legionella clearance across different sources. The persistent positive ice machines prompted implementation of an enhanced sanitization process beyond manufacturer recommendations. This highlights the challenges associated with biofilm control in these devices. Standard cleaning practices based on ice machine manufacturer’s instructions for use (MIFU) may be insufficient at eliminating contamination. These findings support the need for enhanced mitigation strategies and routine environmental surveillance.A table comparing the number of positive samples and median cycles to negative for different water sources.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the persistent environmental reservoirs of Legionella species in healthcare water systems, particularly ice machines, which pose infection risks to immunocompromised patients. It aimed to determine why standard mitigation cycles often fail to achieve sustained Legionella clearance in these devices.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective review of environmental Legionella testing data from 2024–2025 was conducted, including positive results from ice machines, sinks, and showers identified through routine surveillance and outbreak investigations. A total of 18 ice machines and 25 sinks and showers that tested positive for Legionella species were included in the analysis.
analysis.methods: The number of mitigation cycles required for each contaminated source to achieve negative Legionella results was assessed. Environmental samples were collected from water sources, and the clearance of Legionella was tracked across repeated mitigation cycles.
analysis.main_results: Among 367 water sources sampled, 25 sinks and showers (8% of total samples) tested positive and required a mean of 1.66 mitigation cycles, with no fixture requiring more than five cycles. In contrast, 18 positive ice machines (33% of total samples) required a mean of 2.67 mitigation cycles, with one machine requiring eight cycles. ANOVA testing showed no statistically significant differences in the number of cycles to clear Legionella between sources (F(2,40)=2.65, p=0.083).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Ice machines demonstrated a higher frequency of persistent Legionella positivity and required more remediation cycles than sinks and showers, suggesting that standard cleaning practices may be insufficient for these devices. The study highlights the challenges of biofilm control in ice machines and prompted implementation of enhanced sanitization processes beyond manufacturer recommendations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the need for enhanced mitigation strategies and routine environmental surveillance to reduce Legionella contamination in healthcare water systems. Standard cleaning practices based on manufacturer instructions may be inadequate for ice machines, necessitating revised protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of statistically significant differences between source types. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential confounding from unmeasured variables and reliance on routine surveillance data.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated Legionella clearance in healthcare water systems, focusing on ice machines, sinks, and showers. Among 367 samples, 8% of sinks and showers tested positive for Legionella and required a mean of 1.66 mitigation cycles, while 33% of ice machines tested positive and required a mean of 2.67 cycles, with one machine needing eight cycles. Although ANOVA showed no statistically significant differences between sources (p=0.083), ice machines demonstrated higher persistent positivity and required more remediation cycles. The authors concluded that standard cleaning practices may be insufficient for ice machines, prompting enhanced sanitization beyond manufacturer recommendations. The study underscores the challenges of biofilm control in these devices and supports the need for improved mitigation strategies and routine surveillance in healthcare settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了医疗供水系统(特别是制冰机)中军团菌的持续环境储存宿主问题,这对免疫功能低下的患者构成感染风险。其目的是确定为什么标准缓解周期常常无法在这些设备中实现持续的军团菌清除。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 2024 年至 2025 年环境军团菌测试数据进行了回顾性审查,包括通过常规 监测 和 暴发 调查确定的制冰机、水槽和淋浴器的阳性结果。分析中共有 18 台制冰机以及 25 个水槽和淋浴器检测出军团菌呈阳性。
elements_zh.methods: 对每个污染源达到阴性军团菌结果所需的缓解周期数进行了评估。从水源中收集环境样本,并在重复的缓解周期中跟踪军团菌的清除情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 在采样的 367 个水源中,25 个水槽和淋浴器(占样本总数的 8%)检测呈阳性,平均需要 1.66 个缓解周期,没有固定装置需要超过 5 个周期。相比之下,18 台阳性制冰机(占总样本的 33%)平均需要 2.67 个缓解周期,其中一台机器需要 8 个周期。方差分析测试显示,清除不同来源军团菌的周期数没有统计学上的显着差异(F(2,40)=2.65,p=0.083)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与水槽和淋浴器相比,制冰机表现出更高的持续军团菌阳性频率,并且需要更多的修复周期,这表明标准清洁实践可能不足以满足这些设备的需要。该研究强调了制冰机中生物膜控制的挑战,并促使实施超出制造商建议的强化消毒流程。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持需要加强缓解策略和常规环境 监测,以减少医疗供水系统中的军团菌污染。基于制造商说明的标准清洁实践可能不足以用于制冰机,因此需要修改协议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计、样本量小以及来源类型之间缺乏统计上的显着差异而受到限制。由于未测量变量的潜在混淆以及对常规 监测 数据的依赖,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了医疗供水系统(特别是制冰机)中军团菌的持续环境储存宿主问题,这对免疫功能低下的患者构成感染风险。其目的是确定为什么标准缓解周期常常无法在这些设备中实现持续的军团菌清除。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 2024 年至 2025 年环境军团菌测试数据进行了回顾性审查,包括通过常规 监测 和 暴发 调查确定的制冰机、水槽和淋浴器的阳性结果。分析中共有 18 台制冰机以及 25 个水槽和淋浴器检测出军团菌呈阳性。
analysis_zh.methods: 对每个污染源达到阴性军团菌结果所需的缓解周期数进行了评估。从水源中收集环境样本,并在重复的缓解周期中跟踪军团菌的清除情况。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在采样的 367 个水源中,25 个水槽和淋浴器(占样本总数的 8%)检测呈阳性,平均需要 1.66 个缓解周期,没有固定装置需要超过 5 个周期。相比之下,18 台阳性制冰机(占总样本的 33%)平均需要 2.67 个缓解周期,其中一台机器需要 8 个周期。方差分析测试显示,清除不同来源军团菌的周期数没有统计学上的显着差异(F(2,40)=2.65,p=0.083)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与水槽和淋浴器相比,制冰机表现出更高的持续军团菌阳性频率,并且需要更多的修复周期,这表明标准清洁实践可能不足以满足这些设备的需要。该研究强调了制冰机中生物膜控制的挑战,并促使实施超出制造商建议的强化消毒流程。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持需要加强缓解策略和常规环境 监测,以减少医疗供水系统中的军团菌污染。基于制造商说明的标准清洁实践可能不足以用于制冰机,因此需要修改协议。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计、样本量小以及来源类型之间缺乏统计上的显着差异而受到限制。由于未测量变量的潜在混淆以及对常规 监测 数据的依赖,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: With increasing utilization of oral antibiotics in serious infections, complex outpatient antimicrobial therapy (COpAT) programs are vital for improving patient safety and outcomes. We discuss the Michigan Medicine (MM) COpAT program, including processes, interventions, and evaluate its impact. Methods: Adult patients discharged from MM hospital between Jan-Oct 2025 were eligible for COpAT program enrollment if prescribed antibiotics for ≥14 days, including oral antibiotics requiring lab monitoring, long-acting lipoglycopeptides, or intravenous (IV) antibiotics administered at a hemodialysis center, subacute nursing facility, or home. Eligible diagnoses include osteomyelitis, prosthetic joint infection, septic joint, spinal hardware infection and infectious tenosynovitis. Established in October 2024, the COpAT program consists of an infectious diseases (ID) pharmacist with ID physician oversight. The pharmacist conducts a telephone-encounter within 2 business days of discharge to review antibiotic plan, lab monitoring, appropriate antibiotic administration, duration and adherence, and assess for adverse effects. The outpatient ID physician is notified of treatment concerns and lab monitoring results. Another telephone-encounter occurs 2 weeks post-discharge to re-evaluate antibiotic therapy. COpAT patient outcomes and process measures were compared to a historical cohort of patients discharged from MM on oral or IV antibiotics for an osteoarticular infection from May – August 2023. Chi-squared tests were used for categorical variables; the Mann-Whitney U test was used to compare median length of stay (LOS). Results: From January-October 2025, 163 patients with osteoarticular infections were enrolled in COpAT post-discharge. There were 124 patients in the historical cohort. Among COpAT patients, 79.8% (130/163) were discharged on oral antibiotics compared to 33.9% (42/124) in the historical cohort (p<0.0001, Figure 1). COpAT patients had a shorter median LOS of 6.1 days [IQR 4.2-8.7] versus 8.2 days [IQR 5.3-12.1, p<0.0001], and numerical reduction of 30-day readmission rate of 12% (19/158) versus 16.9% (22/132) in the historical cohort (p=0.258). In a subset of 85 patients enrolled from 1/1– 5/31/25, 96.5% had a COpAT telephone-encounter within 2 business days and 638 pharmacist interventions occurred with an average 7.4 interventions/patient (Figure 2). Conclusion: COpAT patients had significantly increased oral antibiotic utilization and shorter LOS, and numerically fewer readmissions compared to a historic cohort. The increase in oral and long-acting antibiotics, rapid post-discharge follow-up and multiple COpAT pharmacist interventions likely contributed to improved outcomes and safer transitions of care. COpAT programs should be instituted to improve patient outcomes and ensure safe use of oral and IV antibiotics in serious infections.A bar graph comparing oral and long-acting antibiotics versus intravenous antibiotics for osteoarticular infections. A bar graph showing pharmacist interventions over five months.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for safe transitions of care for patients requiring prolonged outpatient antibiotic therapy, highlighting gaps in monitoring and follow-up after hospital discharge for serious infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study compared outcomes of patients enrolled in the Michigan Medicine Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) program from January to October 2025 with a historical cohort discharged on antibiotics for osteoarticular infections between May and August 2023.
analysis.methods: Eligible patients were adults discharged on antibiotics for ≥14 days, including oral antibiotics requiring monitoring, long-acting lipoglycopeptides, or IV antibiotics administered at specific settings. An infectious diseases pharmacist conducted telephone encounters within 2 business days and 2 weeks post-discharge to review therapy, monitoring, adherence, and adverse effects, with physician oversight.
analysis.main_results: Among 163 COpAT patients, 79.8% (130/163) were discharged on oral antibiotics versus 33.9% (42/124) in the historical cohort (p<0.0001). COpAT patients had a shorter median length of stay (6.1 days [IQR 4.2–8.7] vs 8.2 days [IQR 5.3–12.1], p<0.0001) and a numerically lower 30-day readmission rate (12% vs 16.9%, p=0.258).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors attribute improved outcomes to increased oral antibiotic use, rapid post-discharge follow-up, and frequent pharmacist interventions, suggesting COpAT programs enhance patient safety and care transitions for serious infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support implementing COpAT programs to improve patient safety and optimize antibiotic use in serious infections, particularly for osteoarticular infections requiring prolonged therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design, reliance on historical controls, and lack of randomization limit causal inference; generalizability may be constrained by single-center data and specific infection types, warranting moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the impact of the Michigan Medicine Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) program on patients discharged with prolonged antibiotic therapy for osteoarticular infections. Compared to a historical cohort, COpAT patients had significantly higher oral antibiotic utilization (79.8% vs 33.9%, p<0.0001) and shorter median hospital stays (6.1 vs 8.2 days, p<0.0001), with a numerically lower 30-day readmission rate (12% vs 16.9%, p=0.258). The program involved structured pharmacist-led telephone follow-up within 2 business days and 2 weeks post-discharge, alongside infectious diseases physician oversight. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that COpAT programs improve patient safety and care transitions by enabling safer use of oral and IV antibiotics. While the results suggest benefits, the study’s retrospective design, single-center setting, and lack of randomization limit causal conclusions, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了需要长期门诊抗生素治疗的患者安全过渡护理的需要,强调了严重感染出院后监测和随访方面的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性 队列研究 研究比较了 2025 年 1 月至 10 月参加密歇根医学综合门诊抗菌治疗 (COpAT) 计划的患者与 2023 年 5 月至 8 月期间因骨关节感染接受抗生素治疗出院的历史 队列研究 患者的结果。
elements_zh.methods: 符合条件的患者是出院后服用抗生素≥14天的成年人,包括需要监测的口服抗生素、长效脂糖肽或在特定环境下静脉注射抗生素。传染病药剂师在出院后 2 个工作日和 2 周内进行电话会面,以在医生的监督下审查治疗、监测、依从性和不良反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 163 名 COpAT 患者中,79.8% (130/163) 因口服抗生素出院,而历史 队列研究 中这一比例为 33.9% (42/124) (p<0.0001)。COpAT 患者的中位住院时间较短(6.1 天 [IQR 4.2–8.7] 与 8.2 天 [IQR 5.3–12.1],p<0.0001),并且 30 天再入院率在数值上较低(12% vs 16.9%,p=0.258)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将改善的结果归因于增加口服抗生素的使用、快速出院后随访以及频繁的药剂师干预,表明 COpAT 计划可增强患者的安全和严重感染的护理过渡。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持实施 COpAT 计划,以提高患者安全并优化严重感染中抗生素的使用,特别是需要长期治疗的骨关节感染。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的回顾性设计、对历史对照的依赖以及缺乏随机性限制了因果推断;普遍性可能受到单中心数据和特定感染类型的限制,需要适度的信心。

analysis_zh.methods: 符合条件的患者是出院后服用抗生素≥14天的成年人,包括需要监测的口服抗生素、长效脂糖肽或在特定环境下静脉注射抗生素。传染病药剂师在出院后 2 个工作日和 2 周内进行电话会面,以在医生的监督下审查治疗、监测、依从性和不良反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 163 名 COpAT 患者中,79.8% (130/163) 因口服抗生素出院,而历史 队列研究 中这一比例为 33.9% (42/124) (p<0.0001)。COpAT 患者的中位住院时间较短(6.1 天 [IQR 4.2–8.7] 与 8.2 天 [IQR 5.3–12.1],p<0.0001),并且 30 天再入院率在数值上较低(12% vs 16.9%,p=0.258)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将改善的结果归因于增加口服抗生素的使用、快速出院后随访以及频繁的药剂师干预,表明 COpAT 计划可增强患者的安全和严重感染的护理过渡。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持实施 COpAT 计划,以提高患者安全并优化严重感染中抗生素的使用,特别是需要长期治疗的骨关节感染。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的回顾性设计、对历史对照的依赖以及缺乏随机性限制了因果推断;普遍性可能受到单中心数据和特定感染类型的限制,需要适度的信心。

papers.full_text: 285 Development of a shared patient registry for measles exposure management amongst multiple stakeholder groups Background Enhanced Barrier Precautions (EBP) aim to reduce multidrug-resistant organism transmission in long-term care settings. Infection preventionists play a critical role in implementing EBP, yet their experiences navigating operational challenges, staff adherence, and resident safety remain underexplored. Understanding these perspectives informs strategies for effective infection control and policy development. Methods A 42-item electronic survey was distributed via Qualtrics to 578 Florida nursing homes between May and September 2024, addressed to “Infection Control.” Ninety valid responses were received. Thirty-seven respondents provided 58 comments across seven prompts—six linked to specific survey questions and one to an open-ended prompt to share questions or thoughts about EBP. Comments were coded into nine categories and analyzed using MAXQDA Analytics Pro. Results The coding categories were: 1) Citation or Feedback, 2) Clarity and Scope of Criteria, 3) Cost and Resource Burden, 4) Effect on Infection Control Practice, 5) Effectiveness of EBP, 6) Resident Experience, 7) Staff Confusion, 8) Staffing, Workload, and Compliance, and 9) Support for EBP. Fourteen coded comments fell under Citation or Feedback, mostly related to corrective feedback or citations during F880 survey experiences, including, “Facility interpreted an action to be low contact and therefore not needing EBP while surveyor considered action to be high contact requiring full EBP”. Staffing, Workload, and Compliance had 13 coded comments, including six responses to a survey prompt asking about challenges in implementing EBP. One respondent wrote, “Non compliance in donning. No one wants to take the time to don when they are strapped for time.” Clarity and Scope of Criteria had ten coded comments, with four specifically mentioning wounds. One wrote, “I think that small skin tears should not be included into the EBP, so there is such a gray area on who should be on EBH [sic] and who doesn’t need to be. So maybe clarify skin tears.” Seven comments addressed Resident Experience, with mixed views on resident reactions. Cost and Resource Burden, Support for EBP, and Effectiveness of EBP each had four comments; Staff Confusion had two, and Effect on Infection Control Practices had one. Conclusions Infection preventionists reported significant challenges in implementing EBP, particularly staffing limitations, unclear criteria, and resource constraints. While many supported EBP’s intent, concerns about feasibility and resident impact persist. Addressing these barriers through clearer guidance, staff education, and resource allocation is essential for successful adoption and sustained infection control in long-term care settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the underexplored experiences of infection preventionists in navigating operational challenges, staff adherence, and resident safety related to Enhanced Barrier Precautions (EBP) in long-term care settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A 42-item electronic survey was distributed to 578 Florida nursing homes between May and September 2024, targeting infection preventionists. Ninety valid responses were received, with thirty-seven respondents providing 58 comments across seven prompts.
analysis.methods: The survey was conducted via Qualtrics, and comments were coded into nine categories using MAXQDA Analytics Pro for analysis.
analysis.main_results: The coding categories included Citation or Feedback, Clarity and Scope of Criteria, Cost and Resource Burden, Effect on Infection Control Practice, Effectiveness of EBP, Resident Experience, Staff Confusion, Staffing, Workload, and Compliance, and Support for EBP. Fourteen comments fell under Citation or Feedback, ten under Clarity and Scope of Criteria, and others were distributed across the remaining categories.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting significant challenges in implementing EBP, particularly staffing limitations, unclear criteria, and resource constraints, which were not previously well-documented.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform strategies for improving infection control practices and policy development by addressing the barriers to effective implementation of EBP in long-term care settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported survey data, which may introduce bias, and the potential for subjective interpretation of EBP criteria. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the challenges faced by infection preventionists in implementing Enhanced Barrier Precautions (EBP) in long-term care settings. A survey of 578 Florida nursing homes yielded 90 responses, with 58 comments across nine categories. The findings reveal significant issues with staffing, unclear criteria, and resource constraints in EBP implementation. The authors suggest that addressing these barriers through clearer guidance, staff education, and resource allocation is essential for effective infection control. While the study provides valuable insights into the practical challenges of EBP, its reliance on self-reported data introduces potential bias, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决感染预防人员在应对长期护理机构中与增强屏障预防措施 (EBP) 相关的操作挑战、工作人员依从性和居民安全方面尚未探索的经验。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 5 月至 9 月期间,向佛罗里达州 578 家疗养院分发了一份包含 42 项的电子调查,针对感染预防人员。共收到 90 份有效回复,其中 37 名受访者在 7 个提示中提供了 58 条评论。
elements_zh.methods: 该调查是通过 Qualtrics 进行的,并使用 MAXQDA Analytics Pro 将评论分为九类进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 编码类别包括引用或反馈、标准的清晰度和范围、成本和资源负担、对感染控制实践的影响、EBP 的有效性、住院医师体验、员工困惑、人员配备、工作量和合规性以及对 EBP 的支持。十四条评论属于引文或反馈,十条属于标准的清晰度和范围,其他评论则分布在其余类别中。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了实施 EBP 方面的重大挑战,特别是人员限制、标准不明确和资源限制,这些以前没有得到充分记录。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过解决长期护理机构中有效实施 EBP 的障碍,为改善感染控制实践和政策制定的策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于自我报告的调查数据,这可能会引入偏差,并且可能对 EBP 标准进行主观解释。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。
