papers.full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Outbreaks Abstract ID: 333 Institutional and Behavioral Determinants of Sharps Injury Reporting and Protective Equipment Use in Nursing Professionals in Croatia Teppei Shimasaki1 Kyorin University Background: Trypan blue is commonly used during mature cataract sur- gery to improve visualization of the anterior capsule. Although FDA- approved since 2004, it remains unapproved in Japan. Many clinics per- form sterile filtration prior to use; however, no standardized sterilization protocol exists. Methods: This retrospective case series included all patients diagnosed with Sarocladium kiliense endophthalmitis after cata- ract surgery at Kyorin University Hospital between 2015 and 2025. Results: In 2025, six microbiologically confirmed cases of S. kiliense endophthalmitis were identified; none occurred before 2024. One case originated from Clinic A and five from Clinic B. All cataract surgeries used trypan blue, which had been sterile-filtered at each institution. Discussion: Endophthalmitis is a rare postoperative complication of cataract surgery, and S. kiliense is an uncommon pathogen. We were informed that similar cases occurred sporadically in 2025 from a reference laboratory center. One institution confirmed contamination of the trypan blue product (unpub- lished data). The same organism was isolated from dye obtained from Clinic B. All affected clinics used trypan blue from the same manufacturer. Off-label product use may pose significant safety concerns due to limited data. While other off-label dyes (e.g., Lugol’s solution, India ink) are widely used in Japan, they are applied superficially. We hypothesize that contami- nated trypan blue migrated into the vitreous cavity via lens zonules, caus- ing the outbreak. Physicians bear responsibility for off-label use and should employ unapproved products only when benefits clearly outweigh risks. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. As a highly infectious virus with an estimated R ranging from 12-18, we sought rapidly scalable and implementable mea- sles preparedness measures for our facilities. Methods: The electronic health record (EHR) has flags that can be placed on patient records to denote the presence of, or concern for, active, transmissible infections. These flags are highly visible in the EHR and represent a good usability heuristic as front line providers are already trained to look for this infor- mation. Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) worked with nursing informatics to develop measles-specific flags for suspected, confirmed and exposed patients in the EHR, expanding flagging functionality in preparation for potential measles cases and exposures. The flagging was tied to registry functionality to allow for tracking of exposed and confirmed cases longitudinally for supporting IPAC investigations in addition to clinical operations. Results: Three different flags were developed in the EHR to address measles. Specific criteria were created for each flag, as shown in Table 1. Table 1: Attached as Image Conclusion: As a highly con- tagious virus, measles presents unique challenges to healthcare facilities managing both cases and exposures. Measles flags within the EHR can be leveraged to assist facilities with case tracking, exposure management, and infection prevention and control. analysis.research_question_and_background: In 2025, measles outbreaks drove 87% of confirmed cases in the United States, highlighting the need for rapidly scalable preparedness measures in healthcare facilities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at Mayo Clinic facilities, where Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) collaborated with nursing informatics to develop measles-specific electronic health record (EHR) flags for suspected, confirmed, and exposed patients.
analysis.methods: The EHR flags were designed to be highly visible and integrated with registry functionality to enable longitudinal tracking of exposed and confirmed cases, supporting infection prevention and control investigations and clinical operations.
analysis.main_results: Three distinct measles-specific flags were developed in the EHR, each with specific criteria for use as outlined in Table 1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the EHR flags as a novel and implementable tool to assist facilities in case tracking, exposure management, and infection prevention and control during measles outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Measles flags within the EHR can inform infection prevention strategies by improving case tracking, exposure management, and real-time response capabilities in healthcare settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report the effectiveness of the EHR flags in reducing measles transmission or improving clinical outcomes, limiting the strength of the evidence to a descriptive implementation study.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the development and implementation of measles-specific electronic health record (EHR) flags at Mayo Clinic to support infection prevention and control during a period when measles outbreaks accounted for 87% of confirmed U.S. cases in 2025. The flags were designed to be highly visible and integrated with registry functionality to enable longitudinal tracking of suspected, confirmed, and exposed patients. Three distinct flags with specific criteria were created to assist facilities in case tracking, exposure management, and infection prevention. While the implementation represents a novel and scalable approach, the evidence provided is descriptive and does not evaluate the flags' impact on transmission reduction or clinical outcomes, limiting the strength of conclusions to feasibility and preparedness.

papers.title: EpiFlowML: A modular framework for standardized and reproducible epidemiological forecasting
papers.abstract: EpiFlowML is a modular forecasting framework designed to standardize how epidemiological time series are prepared, modeled, and evaluated across multiple geographies and data sources. The system provides a harmonized workflow for transforming heterogeneous datasets into consistent, analysis-ready formats, fitting and comparing a range of machine learning (ML) models, and producing structured, reproducible outputs. Each module can be configured independently, allowing users to adapt the workflow to different pathogens or health indicators without modifying core code. The framework integrates standardized data ingestion, preprocessing, model fitting, and evaluation routines that generate uniform outputs suitable for comparison and ensemble development. By aligning these components through configuration files and metadata tracking, EpiFlowML supports transparent, reproducible forecasting across diverse epidemiological contexts. The increasing complexity and volume of forecasting models underscores the need for such standardization (1, 2). A global measles forecasting task was used to demonstrate the framework's functionality. This use case highlights the value of harmonized data structures and standardized evaluation in improving reproducibility and interpretability, as we were able to model 111 countries in the same workflow. The framework and supporting code are fully open source under the Creative Commons 4.0 License, enabling adaptation to other diseases or forecasting applications.

The framework enables the transformation of heterogeneous datasets into consistent formats, supports the fitting and comparison of machine learning models, and produces structured, reproducible outputs. It was demonstrated using a global measles forecasting task, where it successfully modeled 111 countries in a unified workflow. The modular design allows for independent configuration of components, making it adaptable to different pathogens or health indicators without altering core code. The integration of standardized data processing and evaluation routines enhances the uniformity of outputs, facilitating comparison and ensemble development. The study highlights the importance of such standardization in addressing the increasing complexity of forecasting models. However, the evidence is based on a single use case and lacks detailed statistical validation, which limits the confidence in its broader applicability.

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: The U.S. is on track to lose measles elimination status after experiencing the highest number of cases in <30 years. With ongoing transmission and falling vaccination rates, health systems must prepare for measles, focusing on minimizing secondary cases and maximizing prevention. We describe a taskforce approach for comprehensive measles (with a lens towards all-hazard)preparedness across our enterprise. Methods: Our mitigation and preparedness taskforce included four workstreams (Figure 1): Early MMR vaccination for children with international travel: Consistently offer and administer initial or second MMR vaccine, as appropriate, for infants and children travelling abroad. Optimize exposure and testing management: Develop tools to expedite the identification of exposed non-immune patients and optimize processes for high volume testing and result tracking. Optimize screening processes at points of entry (POE): Develop streamlined processes for reliable travel and exposure screening at all enterprise wide POEs. Contingency planning for larger scale exposure events/community spread: Develop post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) delivery procedures to respond to large-scale community exposure events and establish partnerships with local public health (PH) departments. Results: Increase in vaccination for non-immune travelers in primary care: We built an EMR (electronic medical record) prompt into all child visits to screen for travel, which interfaced with vaccine clinical decision support to offer/administer vaccines. From May through 12/28/25 we administered 1325 early MMRs to travelling children (Figure 2). EMR-based report to identify exposed individuals and their immune status: This report allows all sites to rapidly identify patients needing PEP after exposure. We also developed processes for pre-emptive approval for large scale testing, result tracking, and high-volume patient notification. Optimization of Screening and POE with EMR upgrades, PPE kits: We are upgrading our EMR to better integrate travel & exposure screening. We developed additional resources including screening supports for non-English languages and PPE kits for immediate use at POE when patients screen positive. Development of PEP clinics and PH Collaboration: We developed processes to stand up PEP clinics at our hospitals to expedite large volume PEP administration. We worked with PH to outline roles, capabilities and resources for response to community outbreaks, optimized staff fit testing and developed drills across all care settings. Conclusions: Preparedness for highly contagious infectious diseases and emerging PH threats is critical. A taskforce approach provides a structured framework for collaboration and mobilization of resources. By utilizing an all-hazards lens, this framework is broadly applicable for vaccine preventable infections and other infectious threats.A table outlining the 2025 Measles Mitigation & Preparedness Taskforce structure and key tasks. A bar graph showing the administration of early M M R vaccines over time.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the growing concern of measles resurgence due to ongoing transmission and declining vaccination rates, emphasizing the need for improved preparedness strategies to minimize secondary cases and enhance prevention efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in an acute care hospital in Slovakia, focusing on implementing a taskforce approach to measles preparedness. The taskforce included four workstreams targeting early vaccination, exposure management, screening processes, and contingency planning for large-scale outbreaks.
analysis.methods: The taskforce utilized an electronic medical record (EMR) prompt to screen for travel during child visits, integrated with vaccine clinical decision support. They also developed tools for identifying exposed non-immune patients, optimized processes for high-volume testing and result tracking, and created streamlined screening procedures at points of entry.
analysis.main_results: From May through December 28, 2025, 1325 early MMR vaccines were administered to traveling children. An EMR-based report enabled rapid identification of exposed individuals and their immune status, and processes for pre-emptive approval of large-scale testing, result tracking, and patient notification were established.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of the effectiveness of the taskforce approach in enhancing measles preparedness, particularly through the integration of digital tools and structured workflows for vaccination and exposure management.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of digital tools and structured frameworks for measles preparedness, which can be applied to improve surveillance, response, and prevention strategies in healthcare settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single hospital and the absence of quantitative outcomes or statistical analysis. However, the evidence is strong due to the implementation of specific preparedness measures and their direct reporting.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the resurgence of measles in the U.S. due to ongoing transmission and declining vaccination rates. It describes a taskforce approach implemented in an acute care hospital in Slovakia to enhance measles preparedness through early vaccination, exposure management, and streamlined screening processes. The EMR-based prompt for travel screening and vaccine administration led to the administration of 1325 early MMR vaccines to traveling children. The taskforce also developed tools for identifying exposed individuals and optimizing testing and result tracking. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of structured frameworks in improving measles preparedness and response. The study's limitations include its focus on a single hospital and lack of quantitative outcomes, but the evidence is strong due to the direct implementation and reporting of preparedness measures.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决由于 传播 持续存在和 疫苗接种 发病率下降而引起的对 麻疹 卷土重来的日益担忧,强调需要改进准备策略,以尽量减少继发病例并加强预防工作。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在斯洛伐克的一家急症护理医院进行,重点是实施 麻疹 准备工作组方法。该工作组包括四个工作流程,针对早期 疫苗接种、暴露管理、筛选流程以及大规模 暴发 的应急计划。
elements_zh.methods: 该工作组利用电子病历 (EMR) 提示来筛查儿童就诊期间的旅行情况,并与 疫苗 临床决策支持相结合。他们还开发了用于识别暴露的非免疫患者的工具,优化了大容量检测和结果跟踪的流程,并在入境点创建了简化的筛查程序。
elements_zh.main_results: 从 2025 年 5 月到 12 月 28 日,旅行儿童接种了 1325 份早期 MMR 疫苗。基于电子病历的报告能够快速识别暴露个体及其免疫状态,并建立了大规模测试的预先批准、结果跟踪和患者通知的流程。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为工作组方法在增强 麻疹 准备工作方面的有效性的证据,特别是通过数字工具和 疫苗接种 和暴露管理的结构化工作流程的集成。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 麻疹 准备的数字工具和结构化框架的开发提供了信息,可用于改进医疗机构中的 麻疹、响应和预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其只关注单个医院并且缺乏定量结果或统计分析。然而,由于具体准备措施的实施及其直接报告,证据是有力的。

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: The 2025 Measles outbreak has affected over 1900 people across the United States. Close collaborations between public health entities and training institutions can increase public knowledge and trust, promote vaccination, optimize options for testing, and reduce exposures. Methods: The Lexington Fayette County Health Department (LFCHD), Kentucky Department for Public Health (KDPH), and the University of Kentucky (UKY) partnered in February 2025 to develop a comprehensive plan to address measles in Kentucky. Priorities for the partnership were: community and provider education, delineation of roles/responsibilities between the health department and UKY, streamlined pathways for testing and post-exposure management, and centralized communication. Standardized educational sessions were developed and deployed widely to outline testing and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) resources. Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) physicians triaged all testing requests in partnership with the health department using CDC criteria for testing. Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccination campaigns were conducted, focusing on prevention and post-exposure management. For healthcare workers (HCW) at UKY, Epic® electronic health record (EHR) templates and order sets outlining CDC and KDPH algorithms were developed and distributed widely. Results: From March through October 2025, the standardized educational talk was given to 398 public health and medical professionals (Table 1). Six public health and healthcare systems adapted the public health-academic center partnership and protocol to their centers (Table 2). Joint media outreach and education resulted in 32 stories across Kentucky and Tennessee. Three Epic® EHR templates were developed and deployed widely (Figures 1-3). IPAC received and triaged approximately 50 calls/EMR messages from HCW about measles testing, resulting in 4 tests performed at the KDPH State Lab. One test returned positive and there were zero healthcare worker exposures. Immune globulin for PEP was offered to 2 exposed patients, though they declined to receive it (Table 2). MMR vaccinations increased by 16% and 53% in the 0-6 year and 6–18-year age groups, respectively from 2024 to 2025, during the same time periods. MMR vaccination in persons over 18 years decreased slightly (4.5%) (Figure 4). Conclusions: Combining the infrastructure, knowledge, and resources of a state and local public health systems with an academic medical center’s training and community trust can increase measles awareness, vaccination, and optimize resources during an outbreak.A table listing standardized educational sessions with details on dates, training topics, audiences, and numbers reached. A table summarizing public health and academic partnership outcomes related to measles management. A textbox containing a medical form for infectious disease notes, specifically for measles. A screenshot of a medical order set for suspected measles testing and isolation. A textbox containing a template for Measles Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) note. Bar graph comparing MMR vaccine doses administered before and after media and educational campaigns across different age groups.

It focused on public health and medical professionals, with 398 participants receiving standardized educational sessions.
analysis.methods: The partnership developed standardized educational sessions, Epic® electronic health record (EHR) templates, and order sets outlining CDC and KDPH algorithms for measles testing and post-exposure management. These tools were deployed widely to enhance testing pathways and communication.
analysis.main_results: From March through October 2025, 398 public health and medical professionals received standardized educational sessions. Six public health and healthcare systems adapted the partnership protocol. One measles test returned positive, and there were zero healthcare worker exposures. Immune globulin for PEP was offered to two exposed patients, though they declined it. MMR vaccinations increased by 16% in the 0-6 year age group and 53% in the 6–18-year age group from 2024 to 2025, while decreasing slightly (4.5%) in persons over 18 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the collaboration between public health systems and academic institutions improved measles awareness and vaccination rates, with notable increases in specific age groups. This approach was novel in its integration of training, communication, and resource optimization during an outbreak.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that partnerships between public health entities and academic centers can enhance measles prevention efforts, increase vaccination rates, and improve post-exposure management strategies, which have direct implications for outbreak control and public health policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single state and the reliance on self-reported data from healthcare workers. The evidence is moderate, as it provides specific results on vaccination rates and testing procedures but lacks broader generalizability and long-term follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a collaborative approach between public health entities and academic institutions in addressing the 2025 Measles outbreak in Kentucky. The partnership focused on community and provider education, streamlined testing pathways, and centralized communication. Standardized educational sessions were given to 398 professionals, and three EHR templates were developed for measles testing and management. One test returned positive, with no healthcare worker exposures. MMR vaccination rates increased by 16% in the 0-6 year age group and 53% in the 6–18-year age group, while decreasing slightly in adults. The authors concluded that such collaborations can improve measles awareness and vaccination rates, offering a novel strategy for outbreak management. However, the study's scope is limited to Kentucky and relies on self-reported data, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2025 年 2 月至 10 月在肯塔基州进行,涉及列克星敦费耶特县卫生局 (LFCHD)、肯塔基州公共卫生部 (KDPH) 和肯塔基大学 (UKY)。它的重点是公共卫生和医疗专业人员,有 398 名参与者接受了标准化教育课程。
elements_zh.methods: 该合作伙伴开发了标准化教育课程、Epic® 电子健康记录 (EHR) 模板以及概述用于 麻疹 测试和暴露后管理的 CDC 和 KDPH 算法的订单集。这些工具被广泛部署,以增强测试路径和沟通。
elements_zh.main_results: From March through October 2025, 398 public health and medical professionals received standardized educational sessions. Six public health and healthcare systems adapted the partnership protocol. One measles test returned positive, and there were zero healthcare worker exposures. MMR vaccinations increased by 16% in the 0-6 year age group and 53% in the 6–18-year age group from 2024 to 2025, while decreasing slightly (4.5%) in persons over 18 years.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,公共卫生系统和学术机构之间的合作提高了 麻疹 意识和 疫苗接种 率,特定年龄组的增幅显着。这种方法的新颖之处在于它在 暴发 期间整合了培训、沟通和资源优化。

papers.title: MMR and varicella immunization during dupilumab therapy.
papers.abstract: Background: The US Food and Drug Administration recommends deferring administration of live vaccines during dupilumab treatment owing to lack of data on safety and efficacy. Understanding the safety profile of measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) and varicella administration in children taking dupilumab is important to promote appropriate vaccination. Objective: Our aim was to determine the safety of MMR and varicella immunizations during treatment with dupilumab and the impact of dupilumab on MMR and varicella vaccination rates in early childhood. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective review of children younger than 9 years who were taking dupilumab and had available vaccination records. The primary outcome measures were vaccine-associated infections, vaccine-associated adverse events, and rate of immunization. Results: Of the 19 patients who received MMR and varicella immunization while taking dupilumab, none experienced severe vaccine-associated events or vaccine-associated infections. One patient reported fever and injection site reaction, and 5 reported a flare of atopic dermatitis (AD). In all, administration of 21 varicella boosters (9.7%) and 25 MMR boosters (11.5%) were delayed because the children were taking dupilumab. There was a significant delay in the age of administration of MMR boosters and varicella boosters when before- and after-dupilumab therapy rates were compared. Conclusion: MMR and varicella immunization may be safe to administer to children undergoing dupilumab therapy. Pausing dupilumab therapy for administration of live vaccines may lead to flare of underlying AD. Further, dupilumab treatment in early childhood may result in decreased and/or delayed vaccination rates for MMR and varicella. Our findings support the recent recommendation that immunizations not be delayed while patients are receiving dupilumab.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the safety of measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) and varicella immunizations during dupilumab therapy in children and examines the impact of dupilumab on vaccination rates for these diseases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A single-center retrospective review of children younger than 9 years who were taking dupilumab and had available vaccination records was conducted. The primary outcome measures included vaccine-associated infections, vaccine-associated adverse events, and the rate of immunization.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that none of the 19 patients experienced severe vaccine-associated events or infections. One patient reported fever and injection site reaction, and 5 reported a flare of atopic dermatitis. Additionally, there was a significant delay in the administration of MMR and varicella vaccines during dupilumab therapy. The findings support the recent recommendation that immunizations should not be delayed while patients are receiving dupilumab.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that pausing dupilumab therapy for live vaccines may lead to a flare of underlying atopic dermatitis. However, the evidence does not provide detailed information on the long-term safety or efficacy of these vaccines in children on dupilumab therapy.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study highlights the importance of understanding the safety profile of MMR and varicella immunizations in children undergoing dupilumab therapy. It suggests that vaccination should not be delayed during dupilumab treatment, but further research is needed to confirm these findings and address potential long-term effects.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the safety of MMR and varicella immunizations in children receiving dupilumab therapy. A single-center retrospective study of 19 patients found no severe vaccine-associated events or infections, though some mild adverse reactions were reported. The results indicate that dupilumab may lead to delays in vaccination, but the findings support the recommendation to continue immunizations without delay. The study also notes that pausing dupilumab for vaccination might trigger a flare of atopic dermatitis. While the results are promising, the review highlights the need for further research to fully understand the long-term safety and efficacy of these vaccines in this population.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述调查了儿童在 dupilumab 治疗期间 麻疹、腮腺炎、风疹 (MMR) 和水痘免疫接种的安全性,并检查了 dupilumab 对这些疾病的 疫苗接种 率的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 对正在服用 dupilumab 并有可用 疫苗接种 记录的 9 岁以下儿童进行了单中心回顾性审查。主要结局指标包括 疫苗 相关感染、疫苗 相关不良事件以及免疫接种率。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,19名患者中无人出现严重疫苗相关不良事件或感染。1名患者报告发热和注射部位反应,5名患者报告特应性皮炎加重。此外,在度普利单抗治疗期间,MMR和水痘疫苗接种存在显著延迟。研究结果支持近期建议:在使用度普利单抗期间不应推迟疫苗接种。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review investigates the safety of measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) and varicella immunizations during dupilumab therapy in children and examines the impact of dupilumab on vaccination rates for these diseases.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A single-center retrospective review of children younger than 9 years who were taking dupilumab and had available vaccination records was conducted. The primary outcome measures included vaccine-associated infections, vaccine-associated adverse events, and the rate of immunization.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that none of the 19 patients experienced severe vaccine-associated events or infections. One patient reported fever and injection site reaction, and 5 reported a flare of atopic dermatitis. Additionally, there was a significant delay in the administration of MMR and varicella vaccines during dupilumab therapy. The findings support the recent recommendation that immunizations should not be delayed while patients are receiving dupilumab.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that pausing dupilumab therapy for live vaccines may lead to a flare of underlying atopic dermatitis. However, the evidence does not provide detailed information on the long-term safety or efficacy of these vaccines in children on dupilumab therapy.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The study highlights the importance of understanding the safety profile of MMR and varicella immunizations in children undergoing dupilumab therapy. It suggests that vaccination should not be delayed during dupilumab treatment, but further research is needed to confirm these findings and address potential long-term effects.

papers.title_zh: dupilumab 治疗期间的 MMR 和水痘免疫。
papers.source_body_en: Background: The US Food and Drug Administration recommends deferring administration of live vaccines during dupilumab treatment owing to lack of data on safety and efficacy. Understanding the safety profile of measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) and varicella administration in children taking dupilumab is important to promote appropriate vaccination. Objective: Our aim was to determine the safety of MMR and varicella immunizations during treatment with dupilumab and the impact of dupilumab on MMR and varicella vaccination rates in early childhood. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective review of children younger than 9 years who were taking dupilumab and had available vaccination records. The primary outcome measures were vaccine-associated infections, vaccine-associated adverse events, and rate of immunization. Results: Of the 19 patients who received MMR and varicella immunization while taking dupilumab, none experienced severe vaccine-associated events or vaccine-associated infections. One patient reported fever and injection site reaction, and 5 reported a flare of atopic dermatitis (AD). In all, administration of 21 varicella boosters (9.7%) and 25 MMR boosters (11.5%) were delayed because the children were taking dupilumab. There was a significant delay in the age of administration of MMR boosters and varicella boosters when before- and after-dupilumab therapy rates were compared. Conclusion: MMR and varicella immunization may be safe to administer to children undergoing dupilumab therapy. Pausing dupilumab therapy for administration of live vaccines may lead to flare of underlying AD. Further, dupilumab treatment in early childhood may result in decreased and/or delayed vaccination rates for MMR and varicella. Our findings support the recent recommendation that immunizations not be delayed while patients are receiving dupilumab.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)建议在使用度普利单抗(dupilumab)治疗期间,因缺乏安全性和有效性数据,推迟接种活疫苗疫苗。了解度普利单抗治疗期间接种麻疹、腮腺炎、风疹(MMR)和水痘疫苗的安全性,对促进适当的疫苗接种具有重要意义。目的:本研究旨在评估在使用度普利单抗期间接种MMR和水痘疫苗的安全性,以及度普利单抗对儿童早期MMR和水痘疫苗接种率的影响。方法:本研究为单中心回顾性分析,纳入年龄小于9岁且正在使用度普利单抗且拥有疫苗接种记录的儿童。主要结局指标包括疫苗相关感染、疫苗相关不良事件及疫苗接种率。结果:在19名于度普利单抗治疗期间接种MMR和水痘疫苗的患者中,无人出现严重疫苗相关感染或严重疫苗相关不良事件。1名患者报告发热和注射部位反应,5名患者报告特应性皮炎(AD)加重。总计21剂水痘加强针(9.7%)和25剂MMR加强针(11.5%)因患者正在使用度普利单抗而延迟接种。在比较度普利单抗治疗前后的接种年龄时,MMR加强针和水痘加强针的接种年龄均出现显著延迟。结论:MMR和水痘疫苗接种在使用度普利单抗的儿童中可能是安全的。为接种活疫苗而暂停度普利单抗治疗可能导致潜在特应性皮炎加重。此外,度普利单抗在儿童早期的使用可能导致MMR和水痘疫苗接种率降低和/或接种延迟。研究结果支持近期建议:在使用度普利单抗期间不应推迟疫苗接种。

papers.full_text: 54 From Benchmark to Best Practice: Reducing Blood Culture Contamination in Sepsis Care Background: A measles case requires immediate action to identify and administer prophylaxis to exposed individuals in healthcare settings. Infection preventionists (IPs) often balance proactive contact tracing with waiting for a positive test result. Objective: To develop a tool that enables IPs to stratify suspect measles cases by risk level, thereby supporting the decision to prioritize or defer active intervention while awaiting test results. Methods: In spring 2025, we developed a preliminary matrix and used 19 additional suspect patients to further refine the scoring of the tool. In August 2025, we deployed a finalized tool. The two-dimensional risk matrix incorporated both epidemiological risk factors and clinical risk factors, each scored numerically based on yes or no questions. The sum of both categories was used to assign a final risk level that determined the recommendations for IPs (Figure 1). The study population included patients tested for measles during the implementation period. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the distribution of risk categories and outcomes. Among the whole cohort, Firth’s logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between clinical or epidemiological risk score and measles diagnosis. Among the production cohort, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were calculated to evaluate the diagnostic performance. Results: Since implementation, the matrix was applied to 56 patients tested for measles. Of these, 10.7% (n=6) were categorized as high risk, 32.1% (n=18) as medium, and 57.1% (n=32) as low. Four of the 56 patients were positive for measles, 3 were categorized as high-risk and 1 as medium risk. Each one-unit increase in epidemiological risk was associated with a 2 folds increase in the odds of a positive measles diagnosis (odds ratio = 2.0; 95% CI, 1.3–3.6). The low-risk category had an NPV of 1, indicating that all low?risk patients tested negative, thus supporting safe workload reduction by deprioritizing these cases. Conclusion: The Measles Exposure Response Risk Matrix effectively stratified cases and supported IP prioritization efforts. Low-risk groups required no action, expedited testing was reasonable for medium-risk cases, and proactive actions were reserved for high-risk cases. Clinical and epidemiologic risk scores progressed from arbitrary assignment to validated metrics, confirmed by statistical analysis. The flexible design permits adaptation to other infectious diseases, including avian influenza and mpox. With rising measles incidence, tools like this matrix will be essential to support rapid, evidence-based actions by infection prevention teams.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study population included patients tested for measles during the implementation period. The tool was developed and refined using 19 additional suspect patients and then deployed to a production cohort of 56 patients tested for measles.
analysis.methods: A two-dimensional risk matrix was developed, incorporating both epidemiological and clinical risk factors, each scored numerically based on yes or no questions. The sum of these scores determined the final risk level. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the distribution of risk categories, and Firth’s logistic regression was applied to evaluate the association between risk scores and measles diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: Among the 56 patients tested for measles, 10.7% (n=6) were categorized as high risk, 32.1% (n=18) as medium, and 57.1% (n=32) as low. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The Measles Exposure Response Risk Matrix effectively stratified cases and supported infection prevention prioritization efforts. The matrix transformed risk scores from arbitrary assignments to validated metrics, confirmed by statistical analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of risk stratification tools in infection prevention to guide rapid, evidence-based actions in managing measles cases. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发一种工具,供感染预防人员按风险级别对可疑 麻疹 病例进行分层,以便在等待检测结果时就干预优先顺序做出明智的决定。这一背景强调需要立即采取行动,以确定医疗机构中暴露的个人并对其进行预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人群包括在实施期间接受 麻疹 测试的患者。该工具是使用另外 19 名可疑患者开发和完善的,然后部署到由 56 名患者组成的生产 队列研究 中,进行 麻疹 测试。
elements_zh.methods: 开发了一个二维风险矩阵,结合了流行病学和临床风险因素,每个因素都根据是或否问题进行数字评分。这些分数的总和决定了最终的风险级别。采用描述性统计总结风险类别的分布,并应用Firth逻辑回归评估风险评分与麻疹 诊断之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 在接受麻疹检测的56名患者中,10.7%(n=6)被归为高风险,32.1%(n=18)为中风险,57.1%(n=32)为低风险。4名患者麻疹检测阳性,其中3例被归为高风险,1例为中风险。流行病学风险每增加一个单位,麻疹 诊断阳性的几率增加2倍(优势比=2.0;95%置信区间,1.3–3.6)。低风险类别的阴性预测值为1,表明所有低风险患者检测结果均为阴性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 麻疹 暴露反应风险矩阵有效地对病例进行了分层,并支持感染预防优先工作。该矩阵将风险评分从任意分配转换为经过统计分析确认的经过验证的指标。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在感染预防中使用风险分层工具来指导在管理 麻疹 病例时采取快速、基于证据的行动。这些工具对于减少医疗机构中的污染和改善脓毒症护理至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖描述性统计和逻辑回归而受到限制,可能无法完全捕捉风险因素的复杂性。证据是中等的,因为结果基于单个 队列研究 并且该工具的性能是使用一组有限的指标进行评估的。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发一种工具,供感染预防人员按风险级别对可疑 麻疹 病例进行分层,以便在等待检测结果时就干预优先顺序做出明智的决定。这一背景强调需要立即采取行动,以确定医疗机构中暴露的个人并对其进行预防。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人群包括在实施期间接受 麻疹 测试的患者。该工具是使用另外 19 名可疑患者开发和完善的,然后部署到由 56 名患者组成的生产 队列研究 中,进行 麻疹 测试。
analysis_zh.methods: 开发了一个二维风险矩阵,结合了流行病学和临床风险因素,每个因素都根据是或否问题进行数字评分。这些分数的总和决定了最终的风险级别。采用描述性统计总结风险类别的分布,并应用Firth逻辑回归评估风险评分与麻疹 诊断之间的关联。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在接受麻疹检测的56名患者中,10.7%(n=6)被归为高风险,32.1%(n=18)为中风险,57.1%(n=32)为低风险。4名患者麻疹检测阳性,其中3例被归为高风险,1例为中风险。流行病学风险每增加一个单位,麻疹 诊断阳性的几率增加2倍(优势比=2.0;95%置信区间,1.3–3.6)。低风险类别的阴性预测值为1,表明所有低风险患者检测结果均为阴性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 麻疹 暴露反应风险矩阵有效地对病例进行了分层,并支持感染预防优先工作。该矩阵将风险评分从任意分配转换为经过统计分析确认的经过验证的指标。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在感染预防中使用风险分层工具来指导在管理 麻疹 病例时采取快速、基于证据的行动。这些工具对于减少医疗机构中的污染和改善脓毒症护理至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖描述性统计和逻辑回归而受到限制,可能无法完全捕捉风险因素的复杂性。证据是中等的,因为结果基于单个 队列研究 并且该工具的性能是使用一组有限的指标进行评估的。

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: During a measles outbreak in the United States in 2025, health care settings were on high alert for patients who may have been exposed to or infected with this disease. When an infection is found, contact tracing investigations are extensive and require significant labor. Identify, Isolate, Inform (III) has become a standard tool for special pathogen preparedness. Our facility implemented an electronic medical record (EMR) alert for patients reporting fever and rash. The objective of this work is to compare and contrast our experience in drill vs clinical practice. Methods: Setting. Denver Health is an acute-care safety net hospital with both adult and pediatric emergency departments, sharing a common security checkpoint for entrance, and a check in and arrival space before patients are triaged into individual waiting rooms. Drill. In March 2025, Denver Health conducted a drill to test the III process in the pediatric emergency department and urgent care center (PEDUC) where care was provided for a mock patient with fever, rash, and cough. Time to masking and time to isolation were collected by a drill observer. Clinical practice. In April 2025, an infant with recent international travel presented to the PEDUC with cough, fever, and rash and was subsequently diagnosed with measles by PCR. Time to isolation was collected via time stamps in the EMR. Results: During the drill, fever and rash were documented, and the alert fired appropriately. The mock patient was masked within six minutes of entry and roomed in a negative pressure room within nine minutes of entry. During clinical practice, rash was documented, but the patient was afebrile at triage, and the EMR alert did not fire. The patient spent 62 minutes in the waiting room before being roomed. Contact tracing involved individuals in both the adult and pediatric emergency departments due to the shared airspaces. In total, 149 patients were identified as contacts and were notified of the exposure by public health. No transmission was identified. Conclusions: Despite a recent successful drill in the PEDUC, when a patient presented with measles, there were challenges with identification and isolation, as well as structural limitations within the facility and gaps with technology aiding the early identification of patients at risk. Having a real-life situation resulted in an extremely large contact investigation and juxtaposed the recent successful drill, highlighting the need to continue performing “no notice drills” and work on improving each facet of preparedness.Line graph comparing time between arrival and rooming for mock patient and clinical practice.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the practical challenges of implementing the Identify, Isolate, Inform (III) framework during a measles outbreak in a healthcare setting where contact tracing investigations are labor-intensive and resource-demanding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared a simulated drill conducted in March 2025 with a real clinical case in April 2025 at Denver Health, an acute-care safety net hospital with shared adult and pediatric emergency departments and a common security checkpoint.
analysis.methods: The drill measured time to masking and isolation using an observer, while the clinical case recorded time to isolation via electronic medical record (EMR) timestamps. An EMR alert was implemented for patients reporting fever and rash.
analysis.main_results: During the drill, the mock patient was masked within six minutes and isolated in a negative pressure room within nine minutes of entry. In clinical practice, the patient spent 62 minutes in the waiting room before isolation, and the EMR alert did not fire despite documented rash and afebrile status at triage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating that despite a successful drill, real-world implementation revealed structural and technological gaps in early identification and isolation of measles cases, highlighting the need for continuous improvement in preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of refining EMR-based alerts and facility workflows to ensure timely identification and isolation of measles cases, thereby reducing the risk of nosocomial transmission and the scale of contact investigations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the single-center design, lack of randomization, and reliance on observational data, which constrains generalizability and causal inference; the strength of evidence is assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the implementation of the Identify, Isolate, Inform (III) framework for measles preparedness at Denver Health by comparing a simulated drill with a real clinical case. During the drill, a mock patient was rapidly masked and isolated within nine minutes of entry, demonstrating effective preparedness. However, in clinical practice, an infant with measles spent 62 minutes in the waiting room before isolation, and an EMR alert failed to trigger despite documented rash, revealing gaps in early identification. The authors concluded that real-world challenges persisted despite a successful drill, emphasizing the need for ongoing improvement in facility workflows and technology. The findings highlight the importance of timely isolation to prevent nosocomial transmission and reduce the scale of contact investigations during measles outbreaks.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究将 2025 年 3 月在丹佛健康中心进行的模拟演习与 2025 年 4 月的真实临床病例进行了比较。丹佛健康中心是一家急症护理安全网医院,设有共用的成人和儿科急诊室以及共同的安全检查站。
elements_zh.methods: 演练使用观察员测量了掩蔽和隔离的时间,而临床病例则通过电子病历 (EMR) 时间戳记录了隔离的时间。针对报告发烧和皮疹的患者实施了电子病历警报。
elements_zh.main_results: 在演练过程中,模拟患者在六分钟内被戴上口罩,并在进入负压室后九分钟内被隔离。在临床实践中,患者在隔离前在候诊室呆了 62 分钟,尽管在分诊时记录了皮疹和非发热状态,但 EMR 警报并未触发。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,尽管演练成功,但现实世界的实施揭示了在早期识别和隔离 麻疹 病例方面的结构和技术差距,凸显了持续改进准备工作的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了完善基于 EMR 的警报和设施工作流程的重要性,以确保及时识别和隔离 麻疹 病例,从而降低院内 传播 的风险和接触者调查的规模。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据受到单中心设计、缺乏随机性以及对观察数据的依赖的限制,这限制了普遍性和因果推理;证据强度被评估为中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了在接触者追踪调查需要大量人力和资源的医疗保健环境中,在 麻疹 麻疹 期间实施识别、隔离、通知 (III) 框架的实际挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究将 2025 年 3 月在丹佛健康中心进行的模拟演习与 2025 年 4 月的真实临床病例进行了比较。丹佛健康中心是一家急症护理安全网医院,设有共用的成人和儿科急诊室以及共同的安全检查站。
analysis_zh.methods: 演练使用观察员测量了掩蔽和隔离的时间,而临床病例则通过电子病历 (EMR) 时间戳记录了隔离的时间。针对报告发烧和皮疹的患者实施了电子病历警报。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在演练过程中,模拟患者在六分钟内被戴上口罩,并在进入负压室后九分钟内被隔离。在临床实践中,患者在隔离前在候诊室呆了 62 分钟,尽管在分诊时记录了皮疹和非发热状态,但 EMR 警报并未触发。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,尽管演练成功,但现实世界的实施揭示了在早期识别和隔离 麻疹 病例方面的结构和技术差距,凸显了持续改进准备工作的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了完善基于 EMR 的警报和设施工作流程的重要性,以确保及时识别和隔离 麻疹 病例,从而降低院内 传播 的风险和接触者调查的规模。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据受到单中心设计、缺乏随机性以及对观察数据的依赖的限制,这限制了普遍性和因果推理;证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.full_text: 337 Joy of Minimizing Overuse (JOMO): Outcomes of Antimicrobial Stewardship Interventions on Antibiotic Use for Diabetic Foot Infections Background: Measles cases increased significantly in the Americas in 2025; the region lost its measles-free status due to the return of endemic transmission in Canada, Mexico, and the U.S., primarily driven by low vaccination rates among unvaccinated or under-vaccinated populations. In August 2025, Mexico City experienced a surge in measles cases, prompting an urgent call to boost immunization coverage among targeted groups through mass vaccination of children, adolescents, healthcare workers (HCWs), and adults under 50. We report post-vaccination mumps cases among HCWs from six hospitals. Methods: A retrospective study of individuals vaccinated with the Serum Institute of India measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine, which contains the Leningrad-Zagreb (L-Z) strain, was conducted at six national referral tertiary care hospitals affiliated with the Mexican Ministry of Health. We included all individuals under 50 years who, 10-30 days after vaccination, developed salivary gland swelling with or without malaise, headache, lymphadenopathy, or fever. We performed a descriptive analysis and calculated the incidence rate of vaccine-related mumps per 1000 doses of the MMR vaccine. Results: Between 08/21/2025 and 11/30/2025, 10,590 HCWs received the Serum Institute of India MMR vaccine; 27 (2.5 X MMR 1000 vaccines) developed parotid swelling (7 bilateral, 20 unilateral), with concomitant fever in 7 (25.9%); lymphadenopathy, 10 (37%); pharyngitis, 11 (40.7%); arthralgias, 8 (29.6%); and headache, 11 (40.7%). One person developed a rash and malaise. The median time from vaccination to mumps was 16.8 days. No cases of meningitis or other complications were reported. The average duration of symptoms was 8.2 days. No secondary mumps cases were detected. Discussion: Post-vaccination mumps and aseptic meningitis after MMR vaccination are rare and infrequently reported, though prevalence varies by strain. Despite similar efficacy among MMR vaccines, the Serum Institute of India vaccine includes the L-Z strain, which carries a higher risk of mumps (approximately 4.4%) than the Jeryl-Lynn strain used in the MMR-II® (0.5-1.6%), which is primarily used in high-income countries. In our cohort, the prevalence of post-vaccine mumps with the Serum Institute of India MMR, a lower-cost vaccine, was low and consistent with other reports. No cases of aseptic meningitis were reported. With the rising number of measles cases worldwide and the need to increase vaccination coverage against measles in under-vaccinated populations, reinforcing the similar efficacy and safety of different vaccines is crucial. All HCWs must be protected.

papers.title_original: 337 Joy of Minimizing Overuse (JOMO): Outcomes of Antimicrobial Stewardship Interventions on Antibiotic Use for Diabetic Foot Infections

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed because measles cases surged in the Americas in 2025, leading to the loss of measles-free status in Canada, Mexico, and the U.S. due to low vaccination rates among unvaccinated or under-vaccinated populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study was conducted at six national referral tertiary care hospitals affiliated with the Mexican Ministry of Health to investigate post-vaccination mumps cases among healthcare workers (HCWs) under 50 years of age.
analysis.methods: A descriptive analysis was performed, and the incidence rate of vaccine-related mumps per 1000 doses of the Serum Institute of India MMR vaccine was calculated. The MMR vaccine used contained the Leningrad-Zagreb (L-Z) strain.
analysis.main_results: Between 08/21/2025 and 11/30/2025, 10,590 HCWs received the MMR vaccine; 27 (2.5 per 1000 doses) developed parotid swelling (7 bilateral, 20 unilateral), with fever in 7 (25.9%), lymphadenopathy in 10 (37%), pharyngitis in 11 (40.7%), arthralgias in 8 (29.6%), and headache in 11 (40.7%). The median time from vaccination to mumps was 16.8 days, and the average duration of symptoms was 8.2 days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that post-vaccination mumps with the Serum Institute of India MMR vaccine is rare and consistent with other reports, despite the higher risk associated with the Leningrad-Zagreb strain compared to the Jeryl-Lynn strain.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that reinforcing the efficacy and safety of different MMR vaccines is crucial to support increased measles vaccination coverage in under-vaccinated populations during rising global measles cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, lack of a control group, and focus on HCWs, which may not generalize to other populations; the evidence strength is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study at six Mexican tertiary care hospitals investigated post-vaccination mumps cases among healthcare workers under 50 years old who received the Serum Institute of India MMR vaccine containing the Leningrad-Zagreb strain. Between August and November 2025, 27 cases of parotid swelling (2.5 per 1000 doses) were identified, with systemic symptoms such as fever, lymphadenopathy, pharyngitis, arthralgias, and headache. No cases of meningitis or secondary transmission were detected, and symptoms lasted an average of 8.2 days. The authors concluded that post-vaccination mumps with this vaccine is rare and consistent with prior reports, despite the higher risk associated with the Leningrad-Zagreb strain. The findings support the use of this lower-cost vaccine to bolster measles vaccination coverage amid rising global measles cases, though the retrospective design and focus on HCWs limit generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究是必要的,因为 2025 年美洲的 麻疹 病例激增,由于未接种疫苗或疫苗接种不足的人群中 麻疹 率较低,导致加拿大、墨西哥和美国丧失 麻疹 的无状态。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在墨西哥卫生部附属的六家国家转诊三级护理医院进行了一项回顾性研究,调查 50 岁以下医护人员 (HCW) 中 疫苗接种 后流行性腮腺炎病例。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了描述性分析,并计算了印度血清研究所 MMR 疫苗 每 1000 剂 疫苗 相关腮腺炎的 发病率 率。使用的 MMR 疫苗 包含列宁格勒-萨格勒布 (L-Z) 菌株。
elements_zh.main_results: Between 08/21/2025 and 11/30/2025, 10,590 HCWs received the MMR vaccine; 27 (2.5 per 1000 doses) developed parotid swelling (7 bilateral, 20 unilateral), with fever in 7 (25.9%), lymphadenopathy in 10 (37%), pharyngitis in 11 (40.7%), arthralgias in 8 (29.6%), and headache in 11 (40.7%). The median time from vaccination to mumps was 16.8 days, and the average duration of symptoms was 8.2 days.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,尽管与 Jeryl-Lynn 菌株相比,Leningrad-Zagreb 菌株的相关风险更高,但印度血清研究所 MMR 疫苗 的 疫苗接种 后流行性腮腺炎很少见,并且与其他报告一致。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在全球 麻疹 病例不断增加的情况下,加强不同 MMR 麻疹 的有效性和安全性对于支持增加 麻疹 麻疹 疫苗接种不足人群的覆盖率至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计、缺乏对照组以及以医护人员为重点而受到限制,可能无法推广到其他人群;由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.methods: 进行了描述性分析,并计算了印度血清研究所 MMR 疫苗 每 1000 剂 疫苗 相关腮腺炎的 发病率 率。使用的 MMR 疫苗 包含列宁格勒-萨格勒布 (L-Z) 菌株。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,尽管与 Jeryl-Lynn 菌株相比,Leningrad-Zagreb 菌株的相关风险更高,但印度血清研究所 MMR 疫苗 的 疫苗接种 后流行性腮腺炎很少见,并且与其他报告一致。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在全球 麻疹 病例不断增加的情况下,加强不同 MMR 麻疹 的有效性和安全性对于支持增加 麻疹 麻疹 疫苗接种不足人群的覆盖率至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计、缺乏对照组以及以医护人员为重点而受到限制,可能无法推广到其他人群;由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: Cook Children's has two hospitals in North Texas and a network of clinics extending to the West, where a measles outbreak totalling 762 cases began on January 20, 2025. Measles symptoms include fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis before the onset of the morbilliform rash. Timely isolation is recommended for measles. Isolation should continue from four days before to four days after the onset of rash. We hypothesized that contact, travel, and symptom-based screening could prevent amplification of measles in our healthcare settings and avoid positive screens in most neonates with febrile URI. Administratively, screening is unpopular because screening leads to longer registration times, more manpower requirements, and lower patient satisfaction scores. Methods: We selected five measles screening questions employing an adjustable scoring system in which a total score of 5 triggered a positive registration screen, rapid isolation, and further clinician assessment to determine actual testing needs. We scored practice patients by trial and error to settle upon a scheme, then deployed screening at all registration points. We adjusted questions based on evolving local measles epidemiology and redeployed the questions. We monitored throughput. Results: Screening for the first iteration started network-wide on March 31, 2025 (Table 1). Scoring included: 1 point for travel to/living in a measles area; 2 points for case exposure; 1 point for no measles vaccination; 2 points for fever; 1 point for ALL 3 C's – cough, congestion, and red eyes. Not anticipating that parents would answer "UNKNOWN" to some questions, a point counted for those instances. Initially, screen positivity was 0.32% (256 of 80,071), while there were 0 PCR-positive cases. The second iteration (55,603 screens) mended the oversight, reducing positive screens to 0.01%. During a third iteration (70,018 screens) following a visitation to a resort by an outbreak-linked case, "ANY," rather than "ALL of the 3 Cs," and/or rash was counted, increasing screen positivity to 0.03%. After a worrisome non-network case presented without travel or known exposure, a fourth iteration (215,957 screens) increased the maximum to 2 points for each 3C or rash (1/2 point for each), so children without travel or known exposure could have a positive screen. Positivity was 0.01%. For iterations 2-4 (341,578 screens), using measles PCR (n=27) positive as the gold standard, sensitivity was 100%, specificity 96%, PPV 50%, & NPV 100% (Table 2). Using "clinician felt PCR was needed" as a gold standard, clinicians ordered PCR in only 5.7% of positive screens and 0.01% of negative screens, including 3 children with fever and vaccine-associated rash only (Table 4). Registration throughput climbed by 117% but returned to baseline by 2 months (Graph). However, managers were pressed into service directing traffic until screening ended July 27, 2025. Conclusion: Exposure and symptom-based measles screening can avoid positive screens among low-risk febrile neonates with URI. This model should be employed in other areas to prevent measles transmission before the onset of rash.A table comparing measles screening characteristics and trial patients across four iterations. A table comparing the performance characteristics of screening with 5MSQ versus Measles PCR as the gold standard. A table comparing clinician H+P concordance for measles with PCR sent and not sent across multiple iterations of screening with 5MSQ. Line graph showing average registration time per patient and added hours of employee coverage needed for registration at Cook Children's Site: Fort Worth.

papers.title_original: 326 Physician Approach to Indeterminate Clostridioides difficile Test Results

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of managing indeterminate Clostridioides difficile test results in healthcare settings, particularly in preventing measles transmission before rash onset.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at Cook Children's hospitals and clinics in North Texas, including a network-wide measles outbreak with 762 cases starting on January 20, 2025. The population included patients with febrile upper respiratory infections (URI) who were screened for measles.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed a measles screening protocol using an adjustable scoring system with five questions. They iteratively refined the scoring system based on local epidemiology and redeployed it across registration points. They used measles PCR as the gold standard for evaluating screening performance.
analysis.main_results: The initial screening iteration had a positivity rate of 0.32% (256 of 80,071 screens), but no PCR-positive cases were identified. After adjustments, the positivity rate dropped to 0.01% in the second iteration and increased to 0.03% in the third iteration. In the fourth iteration, the positivity rate was again 0.01%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that exposure and symptom-based screening could effectively avoid positive screens among low-risk febrile neonates with URI, and they suggested that this model could be applied in other areas to prevent measles transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that implementing a targeted screening approach can help prevent measles transmission in healthcare settings, particularly in managing cases before rash onset and reducing unnecessary testing.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it relied on PCR as the gold standard and involved iterative adjustments to the screening protocol. The results may not be fully generalizable to other populations or settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of exposure and symptom-based measles screening in healthcare settings to prevent transmission before rash onset. Conducted at Cook Children's hospitals and clinics in North Texas, the research involved four iterations of a screening protocol with adjustable scoring criteria. The initial iteration showed a 0.32% positivity rate, but subsequent adjustments reduced this to 0.01%. The authors concluded that such screening can avoid unnecessary testing in low-risk neonates with febrile URI and recommend its use in other areas to prevent measles spread. The study's findings are supported by PCR as the gold standard, but the iterative nature of the protocol and potential limitations in generalizability suggest a moderate level of evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决医疗机构中管理不确定的艰难梭菌测试结果的挑战,特别是在皮疹发作前预防 麻疹 传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在德克萨斯州北部的库克儿童医院和诊所进行,包括自 2025 年 1 月 20 日开始的全网络 麻疹 麻疹 共 762 例病例。研究人群包括接受 麻疹 筛查的发热性上呼吸道感染 (URI) 患者。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用包含五个问题的可调整评分系统开发了 麻疹 筛选方案。他们基于本地 流行病学 迭代完善了评分系统,并将其重新部署到各个注册点。他们使用 麻疹 PCR 作为评估筛选性能的黄金标准。
elements_zh.main_results: 初次筛查的阳性率为 0.32%(80,071 次筛查中的 256 次),但没有发现 PCR 阳性病例。调整后,第二次迭代的阳性率下降至0.01%,第三次迭代的阳性率上升至0.03%。在第四次迭代中,阳性率再次为 0.01%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,暴露和基于症状的筛查可以有效避免 URI 低危发热新生儿的阳性筛查,并建议该模型可以应用于其他领域,以预防 麻疹 传播。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,实施有针对性的筛查方法有助于在医疗机构中预防 麻疹 传播,特别是在皮疹发作前管理病例并减少不必要的检测。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它依赖 PCR 作为黄金标准,并涉及对筛选方案的迭代调整。结果可能无法完全推广到其他人群或环境。

papers.full_text: 270 3-day Duration for Hospitalized Patients with Community-acquired Pneumonia: Results of a 68 Hospital Survey Background. Clinical identification of measles prompts post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and surveillance. This report informs on implementation, results, facilitators and challenges associated with two measles post-exposure investigations (MPEI). Methods. Two MPEI were conducted in 2025 at a 545-bed public NYC Health+Hospitals. Measles case evaluations utilized the Identify-Isolate-Inform (I3) tool and the MPEI employed Identify-Inform-Initiate PEP-Isolate process (I4). Measles exposure was defined as a person in the Emergency Department (ED) within two hours of the index case. PEP for non-immune exposures was MMR vaccination within 72 hours (immunocompetent), measles intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) within six days (pregnant, immunocompromised), or notification to self-isolate for a 21- to 28-day surveillance period for non-immune persons who did not receive PEP. The exposure window was defined after security tape reviews of ED index-case entries. Epic (Verona, WI) facilitated exposure recalls; a ‘Measles rule out’ banner was uploaded to each chart. Internal and external stakeholders were informed after suspected case isolation. Recalls were conducted using standardized scripts tailored to initial responses and identified accompanying persons. MMR vaccination status was screened for in Epic and NYC vaccine registry. Descriptive analyses were calculated for MPEI. Results. Case 1 presented in Spring 2025 with airborne infection isolation room (AIIR) placement within 16 minutes. Case 2 presented in Summer 2025 with AIIR placement within 10 minutes. Each case had measles serology and nasopharyngeal swab for PCR obtained; the NYC Public Health Laboratory confirmed measles for Case 1 and Case 2 at 28- and 11-hours post-presentation, respectively. There were 145 adults and one child identified in the two MPEI. Spring MPEI identified 70 patients, 11 accompanied persons, 34 staff; Summer MPEI identified 22 patients, three accompanied persons, six staff. Fifty-nine of 146 (40%) exposures were measles immune, 30 received MMR, 3 non-immune pregnant women and one immunocompromised host received measles IVIG; 53 persons were notified to self-isolate through the surveillance period. No secondary cases of measles were identified. Discussion. Each MPEI was initiated after astute identification of a measles case. Key MPEI facilitators were an existing I3 preparedness plan and prior trainings, rapidly defined epidemiological exposure windows, leveraged use of Epic, and a structured post-exposure I4 process. Major challenges were related to uncertainty of a potential surge of cases requiring internal communications for patient flow during the recall process and for streamlined bidirectional communication with public health agencies. We acknowledge limitations of a single-site study and inherent biases of retrospective study design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need for standardized post-exposure management of measles in healthcare settings, where clinical identification triggers post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and surveillance to prevent secondary transmission. It aimed to evaluate the implementation, outcomes, facilitators, and challenges of two measles post-exposure investigations (MPEI) conducted in a large urban hospital system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Two measles post-exposure investigations (MPEI) were conducted in 2025 at a 545-bed public NYC Health+Hospitals facility. The Spring MPEI identified 70 patients, 11 accompanied persons, and 34 staff, while the Summer MPEI identified 22 patients, three accompanied persons, and six staff, totaling 145 adults and one child.
analysis.methods: Measles case evaluations used the Identify-Isolate-Inform (I3) tool, and MPEI employed the Identify-Inform-Initiate PEP-Isolate (I4) process. Exposure windows were defined via security tape reviews of Emergency Department (ED) index-case entries, and Epic facilitated exposure recalls with a 'Measles rule out' banner. MMR vaccination status was screened in Epic and the NYC vaccine registry.
analysis.main_results: Each case had measles serology and nasopharyngeal PCR obtained; the NYC Public Health Laboratory confirmed measles for Case 1 and Case 2 at 28- and 11-hours post-presentation, respectively. Fifty-nine of 146 (40%) exposures were measles-immune, 30 received MMR, 3 non-immune pregnant women and one immunocompromised host received measles IVIG, and 53 persons were notified to self-isolate for 21–28 days. No secondary measles cases were identified.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the absence of secondary cases as evidence that rapid identification, defined exposure windows, and structured PEP protocols effectively prevented transmission. They highlighted facilitators such as pre-existing preparedness plans, Epic integration, and bidirectional public health communication, while noting challenges in patient flow management during recalls.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of standardized I3/I4 frameworks and electronic health record tools to streamline measles outbreak response in hospital settings. They underscore the importance of rapid case confirmation, targeted PEP deployment, and coordinated surveillance to mitigate nosocomial transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations of a single-site retrospective design and inherent biases, which constrain generalizability. Despite these constraints, the evidence is strengthened by target-specific methods, clear exposure definitions, and documented outcomes, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated two measles post-exposure investigations (MPEI) conducted in 2025 at a 545-bed NYC hospital, focusing on implementation, outcomes, facilitators, and challenges. Using the Identify-Isolate-Inform (I3) and Identify-Inform-Initiate PEP-Isolate (I4) frameworks, exposures were defined via security tape reviews and managed through Epic-integrated protocols. Among 146 exposed individuals, 40% were immune, 30 received MMR, 4 received IVIG, and 53 were instructed to self-isolate; no secondary cases occurred. Facilitators included pre-existing preparedness plans, rapid case confirmation, and structured public health communication, while challenges involved patient flow management during recalls. The single-site retrospective design and potential biases limit generalizability, but the target-specific methods and documented outcomes support moderate confidence in the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了医疗机构中 麻疹 标准化暴露后管理的需求,其中临床识别触发暴露后预防 (PEP) 和 监测 以预防继发性 传播。其目的是评估在大型城市医院系统中进行的两项 麻疹 暴露后调查 (MPEI) 的实施、结果、促进因素和挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年,在纽约市一家拥有 545 个床位的公立健康+医院设施中进行了两次 麻疹 暴露后调查 (MPEI)。春季 MPEI 确定了 70 名患者、11 名陪同人员和 34 名工作人员,而夏季 MPEI 确定了 22 名患者、3 名陪同人员和 6 名工作人员,总共 145 名成人和 1 名儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 麻疹 案例评估使用了识别-隔离-通知 (I3) 工具,MPEI 采用了识别-通知-启动 PEP-隔离 (I4) 流程。暴露窗口是通过对急诊室 (ED) 索引病例条目的安全磁带审查来定义的,Epic 通过“麻疹 排除”横幅促进暴露召回。MMR 疫苗接种 状态已在 Epic 和 NYC 疫苗 注册表中进行筛选。
elements_zh.main_results: 每例病例均进行了麻疹检测及鼻咽拭子PCR检测;纽约市公共卫生实验室在病例1和病例2分别于就诊后28小时和11小时确认了麻疹感染。在146例暴露者中,59例(40%)为麻疹免疫,30例接种了MMR疫苗,3例非免疫孕妇及1例免疫功能低下的宿主患者接受了麻疹静脉免疫球蛋白治疗,53人被通知进行21–28天的自我隔离。未发现继发性麻疹病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将继发病例的缺失解释为快速识别、明确的暴露窗口和结构化 PEP 方案有效预防 传播 的证据。他们强调了现有的准备计划、Epic 整合和双向公共卫生沟通等促进因素,同时指出了召回期间患者流程管理方面的挑战。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持使用标准化 I3/I4 框架和电子健康记录工具来简化医院环境中的 麻疹 暴发 响应。他们强调了快速病例确认、有针对性的 PEP 部署以及协调 监测 以减轻院内 传播 风险的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认单中心回顾性设计的局限性和固有偏差,限制了普遍性。尽管存在这些限制,但通过针对具体目标的方法、明确的暴露定义和记录的结果加强了证据,保证了适度的置信度评估。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了医疗机构中 麻疹 标准化暴露后管理的需求,其中临床识别触发暴露后预防 (PEP) 和 监测 以预防继发性 传播。其目的是评估在大型城市医院系统中进行的两项 麻疹 暴露后调查 (MPEI) 的实施、结果、促进因素和挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年,在纽约市一家拥有 545 个床位的公立健康+医院设施中进行了两次 麻疹 暴露后调查 (MPEI)。春季 MPEI 确定了 70 名患者、11 名陪同人员和 34 名工作人员,而夏季 MPEI 确定了 22 名患者、3 名陪同人员和 6 名工作人员,总共 145 名成人和 1 名儿童。
analysis_zh.methods: 麻疹 案例评估使用了识别-隔离-通知 (I3) 工具,MPEI 采用了识别-通知-启动 PEP-隔离 (I4) 流程。暴露窗口是通过对急诊室 (ED) 索引病例条目的安全磁带审查来定义的,Epic 通过“麻疹 排除”横幅促进暴露召回。MMR 疫苗接种 状态已在 Epic 和 NYC 疫苗 注册表中进行筛选。
analysis_zh.main_results: 每例病例均进行了麻疹检测及鼻咽拭子PCR检测;纽约市公共卫生实验室在病例1和病例2分别于就诊后28小时和11小时确认了麻疹感染。在146例暴露者中,59例(40%)为麻疹免疫,30例接种了MMR疫苗,3例非免疫孕妇及1例免疫功能低下的宿主患者接受了麻疹静脉免疫球蛋白治疗,53人被通知进行21–28天的自我隔离。未发现继发性麻疹病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将继发病例的缺失解释为快速识别、明确的暴露窗口和结构化 PEP 方案有效预防 传播 的证据。他们强调了现有的准备计划、Epic 整合和双向公共卫生沟通等促进因素,同时指出了召回期间患者流程管理方面的挑战。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持使用标准化 I3/I4 框架和电子健康记录工具来简化医院环境中的 麻疹 暴发 响应。他们强调了快速病例确认、有针对性的 PEP 部署以及协调 监测 以减轻院内 传播 风险的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认单中心回顾性设计的局限性和固有偏差,限制了普遍性。尽管存在这些限制,但通过针对具体目标的方法、明确的暴露定义和记录的结果加强了证据,保证了适度的置信度评估。

papers.full_text: 35 Etiologic Agents of Non-COVID Community-Acquired Pneumonia Requiring Hospitalization – Analyzing Changes Over Time Background: Measles is a highly transmissible virus. A single case can result in significant exposures within a healthcare facility and prompt action is needed to prevent secondary cases. In October 2025, Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) was notified of a patient being admitted to our facility with recent international travel and symptoms consistent with measles. The patient was unvaccinated and had five healthcare facility visits prior to measles being suspected and subsequently confirmed. Objective: To describe our facility’s effective identification, prioritization, and prophylaxis of individuals exposed to measles. Methods: IPAC leveraged the electronic medical record to identify potentially exposed patients. Patients were quickly assessed for age and immune status, then prioritized and assigned to primary care teams. These teams promptly contacted patients and coordinated PEP administration. Results: Across five encounters, the index patient exposed 539 other patients. Due to delayed notification, our teams had less than four days to administer PEP for those exposed and still within PEP window. PEP administration began within hours of the index case’s positive test and patients received PEP within three days (Table 1). No secondary measles cases occurred within our facility. Conclusion: Timely and coordinated multidisciplinary effort enabled us to rapidly respond to our first measles case and control secondary transmission. Although the index case resulted in a large exposure, patients that were exposed and eligible for PEP were quickly prioritized to prevent secondary transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need to prevent secondary measles transmission in healthcare settings after a single unvaccinated case with multiple exposures. It asked how a facility could rapidly identify, prioritize, and provide post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to exposed individuals to avert nosocomial outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a single-facility outbreak investigation and response study conducted in October 2025. The index patient was unvaccinated and had five healthcare visits before measles was suspected and confirmed. Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) teams assessed exposed patients for age and immune status and assigned them to primary care teams for PEP coordination.
analysis.methods: IPAC used the electronic medical record to identify potentially exposed patients and prioritized them based on age and immune status. Primary care teams contacted patients and coordinated PEP administration within the recommended window.
analysis.main_results: The index patient exposed 539 other patients across five encounters. PEP administration began within hours of the positive test and patients received PEP within three days. No secondary measles cases occurred within the facility.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that a timely and coordinated multidisciplinary response can rapidly control measles transmission in healthcare settings. They highlighted the effectiveness of prioritizing eligible patients for PEP to prevent secondary cases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the importance of rapid identification, prioritization, and PEP administration in healthcare facilities to prevent measles outbreaks. They inform infection control practices for managing measles exposures in unvaccinated populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-facility design and lack of a control group, which constrains generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of comparative data and potential unmeasured confounding in exposure ascertainment.

analysis.summary_en: This single-facility outbreak investigation evaluated the response to a measles case with multiple healthcare exposures in October 2025. The study aimed to describe how exposed patients were identified, prioritized, and provided post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to prevent secondary transmission. Using electronic medical records, Infection Prevention and Control teams rapidly assessed 539 exposed patients and coordinated PEP within three days of the index case’s positive test. No secondary measles cases occurred. The authors concluded that a timely, coordinated multidisciplinary effort effectively controlled transmission. The findings underscore the importance of rapid identification and PEP prioritization in healthcare settings to mitigate measles outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了在单一未接种疫苗病例多次接触后,在医疗机构中预防继发性 麻疹 传播 的公共卫生需求。它询问机构如何快速识别、确定优先级并为接触者提供接触后预防 (PEP),以避免院内感染 暴发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项于 2025 年 10 月进行的单机构 麻疹 调查和反应研究。指标患者未接种疫苗,并在怀疑和确诊 麻疹 之前进行了五次医疗就诊。感染预防和控制 (IPAC) 团队评估了暴露患者的年龄和免疫状态,并将他们分配给初级保健团队进行 PEP 协调。
elements_zh.methods: IPAC 使用电子病历来识别可能暴露的患者,并根据年龄和免疫状态对他们进行优先排序。初级保健团队联系患者并在建议的窗口内协调 PEP 管理。
elements_zh.main_results: 指示患者在五次接触中暴露了其他 539 名患者。PEP 给药在检测呈阳性后数小时内开始,患者在三天内接受 PEP。设施内没有发生继发性 麻疹 病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明及时、协调的多学科反应可以在医疗机构中快速控制 麻疹 传播。他们强调了优先考虑符合条件的患者进行 PEP 以预防继发病例的有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持医疗机构中快速识别、优先排序和 PEP 管理对于预防 麻疹 暴发 的重要性。它们为管理未接种疫苗人群中 麻疹 暴露的感染控制实践提供了信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其单一设施设计和缺乏对照组而受到限制,从而限制了普遍性。由于缺乏比较数据以及暴露确定中潜在的无法测量的混杂因素,证据是中等的。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了在单一未接种疫苗病例多次接触后,在医疗机构中预防继发性 麻疹 传播 的公共卫生需求。它询问机构如何快速识别、确定优先级并为接触者提供接触后预防 (PEP),以避免院内感染 暴发。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项于 2025 年 10 月进行的单机构 麻疹 调查和反应研究。指标患者未接种疫苗,并在怀疑和确诊 麻疹 之前进行了五次医疗就诊。感染预防和控制 (IPAC) 团队评估了暴露患者的年龄和免疫状态,并将他们分配给初级保健团队进行 PEP 协调。
analysis_zh.methods: IPAC 使用电子病历来识别可能暴露的患者,并根据年龄和免疫状态对他们进行优先排序。初级保健团队联系患者并在建议的窗口内协调 PEP 管理。
analysis_zh.main_results: 指示患者在五次接触中暴露了其他 539 名患者。PEP 给药在检测呈阳性后数小时内开始,患者在三天内接受 PEP。设施内没有发生继发性 麻疹 病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明及时、协调的多学科反应可以在医疗机构中快速控制 麻疹 传播。他们强调了优先考虑符合条件的患者进行 PEP 以预防继发病例的有效性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持医疗机构中快速识别、优先排序和 PEP 管理对于预防 麻疹 暴发 的重要性。它们为管理未接种疫苗人群中 麻疹 暴露的感染控制实践提供了信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其单一设施设计和缺乏对照组而受到限制,从而限制了普遍性。由于缺乏比较数据以及暴露确定中潜在的无法测量的混杂因素,证据是中等的。

papers.full_text: 338 Dalbavancin: National Perceptions and Experiences Among Veterans Affairs (VA) Providers Background: Advanced planning and adaptable response strategies are essential for preventing measles transmission in healthcare facilities. Objective: To describe a measles management plan and subsequent modifications in response to a cluster of measles cases. Methods: Drawing on previously published work (doi:10.1017/ice.2025.49), the Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) team initiated a multi-disciplinary team and developed a measles preparedness plan with the following domains: Guidance and education; early detection and testing; isolation and patient movement; contact tracing and exposure management (Table 1). In October 2025, a patient was admitted during their fifth healthcare encounter and was diagnosed with measles. Two family members were later hospitalized with measles. Delayed recognition of the first case prompted enhancements to our preparedness framework (Table 1). Results: The first case resulted in 539 exposed patients. The second resulted in 87 exposures, and the third resulted in no exposure. Despite the extensive exposure, zero secondary measles were reported. Conclusion: Proactive planning enabled rapid response to our first case and controlled secondary transmission. Despite extensive planning, delayed identification of the first case caused significant exposures. As the cluster unfolded, we refined our plan, resulting in zero exposures from the last patient and zero secondary cases, despite over 850 exposures. These efforts may guide other healthcare facilities in improving their measles preparedness and response.
